items.title: The cyclotomic KLR quotient at a dominant integral weight
items.strategy: The idempotents isolate the individual generators, so the displayed ideal also equals $R(\beta)a(x_1)R(\beta)$ when the latter expression is restricted to this block. In the standard choice each isolated generator is homogeneous; this proves the grading, without falsely assigning one degree to their sum. Over a degree-zero field a monic homogeneous polynomial of positive dot degree is the pure power. Lower monic coefficients therefore require forgetting the grading. The example $\lambda_i=2$, $a_i=u(u-1)$ gives $k\oplus k$ at root $\alpha_i$, so its two projective classes cannot be the one-dimensional middle weight of $V(2)$; the standard graded hypothesis is substantive. The rank-zero convention avoids an undefined first letter of the empty word. This definition uses no choice.

items.title: The minimal-parabolic KLR diagram proof category
items.statement:
Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with real simple roots, a field $k$ placed in degree zero, and admissible weighted-homogeneous KLR polynomials $Q_{jk}$ as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. Write $b_{jk}=d_j a_{jk}=b_{kj}$ and fix a color $i$. The **minimal-parabolic KLR diagram proof category** $\mathcal P_i$ is the additive graded $k$-linear category of weighted oriented diagrams with objects weights, downward generators $G_j:\mu\to\mu-\alpha_j$ for every $j$, and the single upward generator $H_i:\mu\to\mu+\alpha_i$. Horizontal composition reads chronological negative words from the vacuum outward. Take additive sums and grading shifts; use idempotent completion when speaking of word projectives. The generator $H_i$ denotes normalized projective restriction: in the polynomial flag realization at input weight $h$, it is basic reversed flag restriction shifted by $-d_i(1+h)$; it is distinct from unshifted basic restriction.

Dots have degree $2d_j$ and downward crossings have degree $-b_{jk}$. The native crossing is $\tau$, with native equal-color divided difference $(f-sf)/(x_1-x_2)$; for expressing the source diagram equations put $\kappa=-\tau$ for **every** color pair, retaining dots, idempotents and $Q$. Thus the native cubic braid numerator is globally opposite to the source numerator, while the quadratic $Q$ is unchanged. Impose the full downward KLR relations of the cited Definition.

At input $i$-weight $h=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$, the first unit $1\to H_iG_i$ and second counit $H_iG_i\to1$ have degree $d_i(1-h)$; the first counit $G_iH_i\to1$ and second unit $1\to G_iH_i$ have degree $d_i(1+h)$. Impose both adjunction triangles with their adjacent input-weight shifts and cyclicity of the dot. For $h\ge0$ prescribe the degree-zero rank-one matrix $H_iG_i\cong G_iH_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{h-1}1\{d_i(1-h+2r)\}$; for $h<0$ prescribe $G_iH_i\cong H_iG_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{-h-1}1\{d_i(1+h+2r)\}$. The off-diagonal crossing component is the cup--source-crossing--cap transfer, and the identity columns/rows are the indicated dotted units/counits. Adjoin its actual inverse blocks, requiring both matrix inverse equations; the dotted dual rows/columns are the finite triangular coefficient convolution determined by bubble inversion, and the crossing block satisfies the local cross-and-cap equations. In particular, at $h<0$, if $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ is this matrix, $r_h^{-1}j_H$ and $p_Hr_h$ are the specified natural inclusion/projection with product $1_{H_iG_i}$.

The normalized far-left bubble series $A_\mu(t),\mathsf H_\mu(t)$ have constant coefficient1 and satisfy $A_\mu(t)\mathsf H_\mu(t)=1$. Genuine negative-degree bubbles vanish. The $A$ coefficient with index $m$ is the clockwise bubble with $-h-1+m$ dots when this count is nonnegative, extended by formal inverse coefficients otherwise; its degree is $2d_i m$. The other family has dot count $h-1+\ell$ and degree $2d_i\ell$. Impose the finite-coefficient slides verified on the monic flag model: adjoining an $i$ root $z$ divides $A$ by $(1-zt)^2$ and multiplies $\mathsf H$ by that factor; adjoining a spectator root $y$ of color $j\ne i$ multiplies $A$ by $q_{ij}^{\rm rev}(y,t)=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$, where $t_{ij}$ is the nonzero extremal coefficient, and divides $\mathsf H$ by it. Every reciprocal coefficient is defined by the finite recursion with constant coefficient1.

Impose the rank-one cross-and-cap equations: the two oppositely oriented single-crossing curls are the signed sums of a dotted uncrossed cap and an opposite bubble over indices $a+b=-1$; the two opposite-crossing cancellations are the straight pair plus the dotted cup--bubble--cap sums over $a+b+c=-1$, with the corresponding opposite-orientation signs. A negative dot count on an open strand is zero. These are the four source $\kappa$ equations, converted globally by $\kappa=-\tau$. For $j\ne i$, the two sideways crossings, defined as the two adjunction mates of the downward crossing, cancel in the two orders with the nonzero scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$; scale the reverse mate by the corresponding inverse to obtain the mixed isomorphism $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$, commuting with the $j$ dot. These are relations of this proof-tool category. Their consistency and homogeneous realization are established by the polynomial flag model, rather than assumed for the actual cyclotomic induction/restriction action.
items.strategy: This is a presentation by generators and homogeneous equations. Check weighted homogeneity of every downward relation using $\deg x_j=2d_j$ and $\deg\tau_{jk}=-b_{jk}$; the global source substitution changes every crossing sign and preserves $Q$. Check the two cup/cap degrees at adjacent weights, giving degree-zero triangle composites and the symmetric identity shifts in both branches of the rank-one matrix. Interpret all fake bubbles and reciprocal slide coefficients by the finite recursion from constant coefficient1, so no analytic series or inverse dot occurs. The local polynomial flag model realizes these equations with normalized $H_i$, shifted spectator flags, explicit dual monic power bases and the actual rank-one inverse blocks, proving consistency. This last well-definedness result is listed in justified_by, while its proof depends on the present definition; it is not a logical dependency of the definition.

items.title: Mixed relations, local nilpotence and weights give the integrable quantum action
items.statement:
Let $V=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}V_\mu$ be a label-weight-graded $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector
space with toral operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee$) acting on $V_\mu$ by
$q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}$, and operators $E_i,F_i$ of weights
$\alpha_i,-\alpha_i$ mapping $V_\mu$ to $V_{\mu+\alpha_i}$ and
$V_{\mu-\alpha_i}$. Assume the toral conjugation and mixed relations, and local
nilpotence of each $E_i$ and $F_i$; vectors have finite label support. Then
these operators uniquely define an integrable type-one
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module structure on $V$ for EVERY real symmetrizable Cartan
datum. Every vector has a finite rank-one $U_i$ orbit and the admissible
Kashiwara $i$-string decomposition applies. Finite weight spaces do not imply
finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ orbits; no such conclusion is asserted.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** finite rank-one reductions: enclose each vector in a finite-dimensional rank-one module, use the rank-one adjoint action on a Hom space to turn $F_j$ into a highest vector, bound its string by the divided-power commutation formula, and read the Serre sum off the surviving coefficient.

1.1 Finite rank-one orbits. Fix $i$ and $v\in V$. Then $W:=\operatorname{span}\{F_i^aE_i^bK_i^cv:a,b\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z\}$ is a finite-dimensional $A_i$-stable subspace, where $A_i$ is the algebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$: the toral operator $K_i$ acts diagonally on the finitely many nonzero label components of $v$, so the vectors $K_i^cv$ span a finite-dimensional subspace; by [A3] there is $B$ with $E_i^bv=0$ for $b\ge B$; the mixed relation of [A2] rewrites any word in $E_i,F_i$ as a linear combination of words $F_i^aE_i^b$ with coefficients in the algebra generated by $K_i$; and one may choose finitely many $K_i^cv$ spanning the toral orbit and use local nilpotence of $F_i$ on their finitely many $E_i^b$-images to bound $a$. The span of the resulting finite set is stable under $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$. [A1, A2, A3]

2.1 The second finite module. Fix $i\ne j$ and set $W':=\operatorname{span}\{F_i^aE_i^bK_i^cF_jw:w\in W,\ a,b\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z\}$. Since $W$ is finite-dimensional, step 1.1 applied to each of the finitely many vectors $F_jw$ exhibits $W'$ as a finite union of finite-dimensional $A_i$-stable subspaces; hence $W'$ is a finite-dimensional $A_i$-stable subspace of $V$ containing $F_jW$. [step 1.1, A1, A2, A3]

3.1 The rank-one adjoint module. On the finite-dimensional space $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$ define operators by $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)(T)=K_iTK_i^{-1}$, $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)(T)=(E_iT-TE_i)K_i$ and $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)(T)=F_iT-K_iTK_i^{-1}F_i$. Substituting these formulas, using $K_iE_i=q_i^2E_iK_i$, $K_iF_i=q_i^{-2}F_iK_i$ and $E_iF_i-F_iE_i=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ on $W,W^{\prime}$, gives $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)^{-1}=q_i^2\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)$, $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)^{-1}=q_i^{-2}\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ and $[\mathrm{Ad}(E_i),\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)]=(\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)-\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. Thus these formulas give a rank-one module directly. Moreover $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)$ is diagonalizable because $K_i$ acts diagonally on $W$ and $W'$, and $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i),\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ are locally nilpotent: $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)$ raises and $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ lowers the $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)$-weight by $2$, the weights of $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$ form a finite set, and decomposing any $T$ into weight components each orbit is supported on distinct weights and hence terminates. [A1, A2, step 2.1]

4.1 $F_j$ is a highest vector of weight $m$. Since $F_jW\subseteq W'$, the restriction $T:=F_j|_W$ lies in $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$. By [A2], $E_iF_j=F_jE_i$ for $i\ne j$, so $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)(T)=(E_iT-TE_i)K_i=0$; and by [A1], $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)(T)=K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}T$, because $\langle\alpha_j,d_ih_i\rangle=d_ia_{ij}$. Put $m:=-a_{ij}\ge0$, the off-diagonal Cartan entries being nonpositive. Thus $T$ is annihilated by $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)$ and has $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)$-weight $q_i^m$ with $m\ge0$. [A1, A2, step 3.1]

5.1 The rank-one string bound. Assume $T\ne0$. In the rank-one module $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$ of steps 3.1-4.1 let $t\ge1$ be minimal with $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^tT=0$; it exists by the local nilpotence of step 3.1. For $b\ge1$ the divided-power formula of [F3] gives $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{(b)}(T)=\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{(b-1)}\Theta_{i,b}(T)$, and $\Theta_{i,b}$ acts on $T$ by the scalar $\frac{1}{q_i^b-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}(q_i^{m-2s}-q_i^{-m+2s})=\frac{q_i^{m-b+1}-q_i^{-m+b-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}=[m-b+1]_i$, by summing the two geometric progressions. Taking $b=t$ and using $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^tT=0$ together with $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{(t-1)}T=[t-1]_i!^{-1}\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{t-1}T\ne0$ gives $[m-t+1]_i=0$, hence $m-t+1=0$ by [F2], that is $t=m+1$; therefore $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{m+1}T=0$. [F2, F3, step 4.1]

6.1 The Serre sum. By induction on $n\ge0$, using $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)(T)=q_i^mT$ and the Pascal recurrence of [F4], the powers of the adjoint action expand as $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^n(T)=\sum_{r=0}^{n}(-1)^rq_i^{r(m-n+1)}\binom{n}{r}_iF_i^{n-r}TF_i^r$: the case $n=0$ is clear, and applying $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ to the formula for $n$, conjugating $K_iF_i^{n-r}TF_i^rK_i^{-1}=q_i^{m-2n}F_i^{n-r}TF_i^r$ and comparing the coefficient of $F_i^{n+1-r}TF_i^r$ uses exactly $C_{n+1,r}=q_i^rC_{n,r}+q_i^{r-n-1}C_{n,r-1}$, the second form of [F4]. At $n=m+1=1-a_{ij}$ every Laurent exponent $r(m-n+1)$ is zero, so step 5.1 gives $\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r=0$ on $W$. Since every $v\in V$ lies in such a $W$ by step 1.1, the negative Serre relation holds as an operator on all of $V$. [F4, step 1.1, step 5.1]

7.1 The positive Serre relation. Put $E_i':=F_i$, $F_i':=E_i$ and $K_h':=K_{-h}$ for all $i$ and $h$. The primed data again satisfies the toral, toral-action, mixed and local-nilpotence hypotheses [A1]-[A3]: for instance $K_h'E_i'K_h'^{-1}=K_{-h}F_iK_h=q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i=q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i'$, while $E_i'F_i'-F_i'E_i'=F_iE_i-E_iF_i=-(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})=(K_i'-K_i'^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. Applying steps 1.1-6.1 to the primed data gives $\sum_{r}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r=0$ on $V$, which is the positive Serre relation for the original data. [A1, A2, A3, step 6.1]

8.1 Conclusion. By [A1]-[A3] the operators satisfy all the defining relations of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$: the toral and toral-action relations, the mixed commutators, and both Serre families by steps 6.1 and 7.1. Hence the universal property [F1] equips $V$ with a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module structure; it is unique because $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is generated by these operators, and it is a chosen $P$-graded type-one weight module by construction. Local nilpotence is exactly [A3], so the module is integrable, and by [F5] the admissible $i$-string decomposition applies to every vector; step 1.1 supplies the finite rank-one $U_i$ orbit. No finite-dimensionality of the full weight spaces is asserted or used. [A3, F1, F5, step 1.1, step 6.1, step 7.1] ∎

items.title: Cyclotomic KLR induction and restriction functors
items.statement: Use the standard graded quotient of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]. Put $A=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $B=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ and $e=e(\beta,i)$. Right append defines a graded CORNER homomorphism $\iota_i:A\to eBe$, sending $1_A$ to $e$, $e(\nu)$ to $e(\nu i)$, and the old dots/crossings to their positions in the first $|\beta|$ strands. It is not asserted injective and $e$ may be zero. Define $F_i^{\rm basic}(M)=Be\otimes_A M$ and $E_i^{\rm basic}(N)=eN$. These additive functors preserve shifts and satisfy $F_i^{\rm basic}\dashv E_i^{\rm basic}$ by degree-zero tensor-Hom evaluation. $F_i$ increases ROOT degree by $\alpha_i$ and decreases module weight $\Lambda-\beta$ by $\alpha_i$; restriction does the reverse. Both composites are endofunctors at a fixed root degree. The same underlying definitions apply ungraded to monic deformations. Exactness/projective preservation and the shifted second adjunction are theorems below.
items.strategy: Each generic generator relation is preserved in the corner, and the first-strand cyclotomic generator maps into the longer ideal. This gives a homomorphism with unit image $e$, not a global-unit inclusion. For example $\lambda_i=1$, $\beta=\alpha_i$ has $A=k$, $B=0$, so the corner homomorphism and induction are zero. Evaluation at $e$ identifies $\operatorname{HOM}_B(Be,N)$ with $eN$, proving the ordinary adjunction with its actual grading. Finite balanced tensors give additivity/shift compatibility. No unshifted second adjunction is assumed; its explicit shift is supplied by the coherent-adjunction lemma.

items.title: Cyclotomic dot annihilators, finite-dimensional blocks, and finite root strings
items.statement: Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)–(Q4) for a real symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree $\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the resulting ordinary quotient. Every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic annihilator in each fixed block, every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over $k$, and, for fixed $\beta,i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.
items.strategy:
Use the exact native presentation, and abbreviate its globally opposite source crossing by $\kappa_a=-\tau_a$ for every color pair; the dots, idempotents and $Q$ do not change. For equal adjacent colors put $x=x_a,y=x_{a+1}$ and $\partial f=(s_af-f)/(x-y)$. If $fe(\nu)$ annihilates a module, the source nil-Hecke identities give $(x-y)\kappa_a f\kappa_a e(\nu)=(s_af-f)\kappa_a e(\nu)=(\kappa_af-\partial f-f\kappa_a)e(\nu)$. The terms containing $f$ vanish, so $\partial f$ vanishes; then $s_af=f+(x-y)\partial f$ also vanishes. This proves annihilator closure under the divided difference and exchange without division by an integer. A common monic annihilator of the first dot is $g_1=\prod_j a_j$, with the zero corners understood in the same way.

Suppose a common monic $g$ of degree $d$ annihilates $x_a$. Equal-color exchange gives $g(y)=0$. At an unequal pair $j,l$, $\kappa_ag(x)\kappa_a=g(y)Q_{jl}(x,y)=0$. Set $C=k[x]/g$, finite free of rank $d$. Multiplication by $Q_{jl}(x,y)$ on $C[y]$ has matrix $M(y)$ with leading coefficient $c\,\mathrm{Id}$ and degree $-a_{lj}$ in $y$, where $c=t_{j,l;0,-a_{lj}}\ne0$. Its determinant $r(y)$ has leading coefficient $c^d$. Applying $\operatorname{adj}(M)M=r\,\mathrm{Id}$ to the vector $1$ gives $Q_{jl}(x,y)R(x,y)\equiv r(y)\pmod {g(x)}$. Thus $g(y)r(y)$ annihilates the corner; divide its leading scalar to obtain a monic polynomial. If $d=0$ that corner is zero; if $a_{lj}=0$, $r=c^d$ is a unit. Take the product over the finite words/pairs and induct over positions. PBW then reduces each dot exponent below its monic bound, leaving finitely many permutations, words and exponent tuples, so the block is finite dimensional. This is a direct ordinary-algebra argument for arbitrary monic polynomials, including $u(u-1)$, rather than a flat-specialization claim.

For standard powers one can strengthen the bounds to nilpotence. If $x^N=0$ and the neighboring colors differ, write $Q_{jl}(x,y)=c y^q+xH(x,y)$, $q=-a_{lj}$, using homogeneity and Q4. The quadratic relation gives $y^NQ=0$, hence $y^{N+q}=-c^{-1}xy^NH$ on the corner. Raising this commuting-polynomial equality to the $N$th power gives $y^{N(N+q)}=0$. Equal-color exchange preserves the exponent $N$. Starting with a common first-strand power proves nilpotence of every dot.

For finite root strings in either branch fix a prefix length $\ell$ and a common monic annihilator $g$ of degree $d$ for $x_{\ell+1}$ in the finite length-$\ell+1$ quotient. Its image annihilates that dot in every longer quotient, since right concatenation preserves the first-strand ideal. In an all-$i$ tail of length $d+1$ starting at position $\ell+1$, repeated annihilator closure gives $\partial_{\ell+d}\cdots\partial_{\ell+1}g(x_{\ell+1})=(-1)^d$, so the tail is zero. Equivalently, in native nil-Hecke rank $s>d$, multiply $g(x_1)$ by $x_1^{s-1-d}x_2^{s-2}\cdots x_{s-1}$. Its top term is the Artin staircase and its lower terms have smaller total degree; the native $\partial_{w_0}$ sends it to $1$. Thus $\partial_{w_0}$ and the full staircase idempotent belong to the ideal generated by $g$. The finite matrix units from the perfect Artin pairing put $1$ in that ideal. Both computations use unit diagonal elimination, never $s!^{-1}$.

Finally induct on the number $b$ of non-$i$ entries. Let $k=L_{b-1}$ be the previous bound and $\ell=b-1+k$. Choose an all-$i$ tail bound $m$ at that prefix length and set $L_b=k+m-1$. A word of length $b+L_b=\ell+m$ with at least $L_b$ copies of $i$ either has at least $k$ in its first $\ell$ positions, whose prefix is already zero, or has at most $k-1$ there and therefore all last $m$ positions are $i$. That tail is zero. A longer word with at most $b$ other colors has a zero initial segment of length $b+L_b$. For fixed $\beta$, $b=\sum_{j\ne i}\beta_j$, so $\beta_i+m\ge L_b$ kills every word in $\beta+m\alpha_i$. The prefix never has to end in color $i$. All constructions involve finite products, determinants, polynomial reductions and integer choices.

items.title: Generic KLR induction and restriction: mixed relations and the opposite-end exact sequence
items.statement:
Let $R=\bigoplus_\beta R(\beta)$ be a KLR algebra on a symmetrizable Cartan datum
with no imaginary simple roots
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]) and let
$E_i$ denote restriction $e(\beta,i)(-)$ and $F_i$, $\bar F_i$ the right-append
and left-append inductions of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]
(so that $\bar F_i(M)=R(\beta+\alpha_i)e(i,\beta)\otimes_{R(\beta)}M$ with
$e(i,\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(i\ast\nu)$). Let $t_i$ be an indeterminate of
degree $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2d_i$. Then:

(a) for $i\ne j$ there are natural isomorphisms
$E_iF_j\cong q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_j)}F_jE_i$ and
$\bar F_jE_i\cong E_i\bar F_j$;

(b) for $i=j$ there is a natural isomorphism
$E_iF_i\cong q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)}F_iE_i\oplus(\mathrm{Id}\otimes_kk[t_i])$,
where $(\mathrm{Id}\otimes_kk[t_i])(M)=M\otimes_kk[t_i]$ with $t_i$ homogeneous
of degree $2d_i$;

(c) the opposite-end corner comparison gives a functorial exact sequence in
$\mathrm{Mod}(R(\beta))$
$$0\longrightarrow \bar F_iE_iM\longrightarrow E_i\bar F_iM\longrightarrow q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)}M\otimes_kk[t_i]\longrightarrow 0,$$
where $\otimes_kk[t_i]$ is understood in the graded sense. For $n\ge1$, the underlying uncolored bimodules have the exact sequence
$0\to R(n)\otimes_{R_1(n-1)}R_1(n)\to R(n+1)\to R(n)\otimes_kk^I[t]\to0$,
where $k^I=\bigoplus_{j\in I}k\epsilon_j$ retains the transferred strand color,
and the right $R(n)$ action is through the shift embedding $\xi_n$.
The quotient grading is the degree of the full transfer word on each labeled
corner; its fixed-color $i$ corner is the shifted polynomial term of (c). All shifts are computed in the fixed grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]; the functors are exact
([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]]).
items.strategy: Use both same-end PBW double cosets: x tensor y maps to x kappa_n y, with kappa=-tau_native and the correct weight gamma=beta-alpha_i+alpha_j. Opposite-end overlap multiplication has all cosets a>=2 as image and the full first-to-last transfer coset as quotient, retaining k^I labels. The coefficient quotient is right split before tensoring. Fixed-color quotient has shift -(alpha_i|beta) and dot degree 2d_i. Verify beta=0 directly from R(0)=k and one-letter polynomial corners; only the uncolored n-1 notation requires n>=1.

items.title: The minimal-parabolic polynomial flag model realizes the graded diagram relations
items.statement:
Fix a color $i$ and the formal proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], on a symmetrizable real
Cartan datum with finite index set and arbitrary field $k$. Use the native KLR
parameters of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], degrees of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], the PBW convention of
[[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]], and the nil-Hecke matrix/idempotent convention
of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Then the polynomial
flag construction described below realizes all the defining graded diagram
relations of that formal category, including its rank-one cross/cap,
bubble-slide/inversion and mixed-color cup/cap relations; it asserts a
representation of the formal proof category, not faithfulness or a cyclotomic
quotient identification.

**The model.** Choose a color order with $i$ last. For spectator alphabets
$Y_j$ of sizes $m_j$ ($j\ne i$) put $C=\bigotimes_{j\ne i}k[Y_j]^{S_{m_j}}$,
$r=m_i$, $A_{ij}=-a_{ij}$,
$t_{ij}=[u^{A_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$,
$q_{ij}=Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$, and choose a monic framing polynomial $a_i(u)$ of
degree $\lambda_i$; initially its coefficients have their universal homogeneous
degrees, so all formulas are graded, and the standard specialization is
$a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. Set
$$p_m(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}q_{ij}(u,y),\qquad N=\lambda_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j,\qquad h_m=N-2r,$$
and $c_r(u)=u^r-e_1u^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^re_r$. The vertex ring $L_m$ is the
monic factor ring for $p_m=c_rb_{N-r}$, equivalently $C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]$ modulo
all coefficients beyond degree $N-r$ of the monic expansion $p_m/c_r$; it is
finite free over $C$ of rank $\binom Nr$ and is zero for $r>N$. Its $i$ flag is
$B_m=L_m[z]/b_{N-r}(z)$, free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over
$L_{m+i}$, with the target root alphabet obtained by adjoining $z$. The
underlying spectator flag is $C_m^j=L_m[y]$; its target action appends $y$ to
$Y_j$ and replaces $p_m$ by $p_mq_{ij}(u,y)$.

**The shifts and generators.** Every downward generator carries the ordered
shift $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$. Thus
$G_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is the $B_m\{-2d_ir\}$ tensor functor; $G_j$ for
$j\ne i$ is the $C_m^j\{s_j(m)\}$ tensor functor. The basic reversed $i$ flag
is $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}=B_m\otimes_{L_{m+i}}-$ without a shift, whereas the
formal upward generator at INPUT vertex $m$ is
$H_i(m)=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(m)\{-d_i(1+h_m)\}$. These are distinct
conventions. The basic flags have degree-zero
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\{t_i(m)\}\dashv F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$, where
$t_i(m)=-2d_i(h_m-1)$. At vertex $m$ the formal first unit and second cap have
degree $d_i(1-h_m)$, and the formal first cap and second unit have degree
$d_i(1+h_m)$.

**The four maps and the Casimir.** All four maps are the explicit dual-basis
maps of the two monic coefficient forms on $B_m$: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}:B_m\to
L_m$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$;
$\tau_{\mathrm{new}}:B_m\to L_{m+i}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$.
The first cap is $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto\tau_{\mathrm{new}}(b_1b_2)$ and the
first cup is its dual-power-basis Casimir; the second cap and cup use
$\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$. For a monic polynomial $f$ their Casimir is the
polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the two-root quotient.

**Crossings, colors and bubbles.** Source crossings are
$\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for EVERY color pair. Source equal-color
operators are $(s-1)/(X-Y)$; source unequal operators are the switch/quotient
in the increasing-color direction and switch times $Q$ in the reverse
direction. Thus native operators are their negatives, and both actual crossing
degrees are $-b_{jk}$ with the ordered shifts above. On the $i,j$ pair the
successive underlying rings are
$D_1=L_m[y,z]/(b(z)q_{ij}(z,y))$ and $D_0=L_m[y,z]/b(z)$, with source maps
$\pi:D_1\to D_0$ and $f\mapsto Q_{ij}(z,y)f:D_0\to D_1$; their normalized
opposite-sideways composites have the scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$, and in the
NE/SW-$i$, NW/SE-$j$ source orientation the double-mate ratio is
$t_{ji}/t_{ij}$. Native minus signs leave the two-crossing scalars and the
ratio unchanged. The basic isomorphism $E_iG_j\cong(G_jE_i)\{-b_{ij}\}$ holds,
and the normalized formal $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$ is unshifted.

**Realized equations.** The canonical rank-one $\rho$ and its inverse, the
same-color cross/cap equations, the bubble series
$\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ and its reciprocal, and the finite-coefficient
bubble-slide identities are realized by the stated polynomial maps. In
particular the normalized positive $h$ identity columns have degrees
$d_i(1-h+2k)$ for $0\le k<h$, and the negative branch uses the inverse
crossing plus the dot/cap rows. All polynomial pairings and relations persist
after arbitrary monic coefficient specialization as UNGRADED identities; such
a specialization does not assert nilpotence, a homogeneous trace degree, or a
highest-weight $K_0$ claim. No geometry, characteristic restriction, or
one-dimensional-Hom hypothesis is imposed.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** constructive: build the monic splitting rings and their Artin bases, define the flag modules and the four coefficient maps, compute the rank-one intertwiner and its inverse by monic division, and verify each family of formal relations by the displayed polynomial identities.

1.1 Monic splitting and the vertex ring. Over the universal coefficient ring $S=k[c_1,\dots,c_N]$, adjoin roots of the monic framing polynomial one at a time and divide by the root: at step $s$ the residual polynomial is monic of degree $N-s+1$, so ordinary monic division preserves monicity. This produces the Artin basis $X_1^{a_1}\cdots X_N^{a_N}$, $0\le a_k\le N-k$, of the full root algebra; the pairing that reads the top coefficient has Gram matrix zero below the anti-diagonal and unit anti-diagonal in reversed order, hence is perfect over $S$, with no factorial division and no characteristic hypothesis. Block decomposition into the $r$ roots of $c_r$ and the $N-r$ roots of $b_{N-r}$ makes $L_m$ finite free over $C$ of rank $\binom Nr$, and $L_m=0$ for $r>N$ because then $p_m$ has degree below $r$. [F1, F2, F3, construct]

2.1 The vertex ring as a matrix quotient. Representing $\mathrm{NH}_r$ as the matrix algebra on its Artin module (step 1.1, [F2]) shows that the two-sided ideal generated by a monic $p(X_1)$ is the matrix ideal of the coefficients of the remainder of $p$ modulo $c_r$, and monic division makes these coefficients a unit triangular change from the consecutive relations; hence $\mathrm{NH}_r/(p(X_1))$ is the matrix algebra over the monic factor ring $L_m$ of the Statement. The same computation shows the $i$-flag $B_m$ is free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over $L_{m+i}$, giving the two root extensions of the model. [step 1.1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 The four coefficient maps and their triangles. For a monic $f$, the polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ is defined before imposing $f(X)=f(Y)=0$ and satisfies $(X-Y)K_f=f(X)-f(Y)$ and $\tau_XK_f=1$; therefore $\tau_X(X^aK_f)=Y^a$ for every $a$, which identifies $K_f$ with the dual-power-basis Casimir of the two monic coefficient forms. The two Casimirs of $b_{N-r}$ and $c_{r+1}$ give the four displayed cups and caps; their contractions are the identities $\sum_av_a\tau(z^ab)=b$ and $\sum_a\tau(bv_a)z^a=b$ for dual Artin bases, and substituting them into the tensor composites proves both triangles of each of the two adjunctions. Degrees: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$; $\tau_{\mathrm{new}}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$; the first maps have degree $0$ after the $B\{-2d_ir\}$ shift; the second cap has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)+2d_ir=-2d_i(h_m-1)$, with inverse degree on its unit. Restoring the normalized $H_i$ at its input weight produces exactly the four formal degrees of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]]. [step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The rank-one intertwiner and its inverse. Splitting off one extra $i$-strand by the two-coset PBW decomposition [F3] gives the transfer term $\kappa_rb$ and the new-dot algebra as its complement; the rank-one intertwiner $g=(u-X)-(u-X)^2\kappa$ is verified to satisfy its quadratic and dot-commutation identities by expanding $\kappa X_{r+1}-X_r\kappa=1$ and $\kappa^2=0$. Multiplying these intertwiners along the extra strand and the other transfer by $p(X_1)$, then projecting to the polynomial complement, yields a coefficient map $A$ with $A(u^kS_r)=(-1)^ru^kp(u)$ where $S_r(u)=\prod_{a\le r}(u-X_a)^2$, and the same mixed relation gives $\phi_{k+1}(u)=u\phi_k+E(\psi_k)$; hence $A(u^k)=(-1)^r\operatorname{quo}_{S_r}(u^kp)$ by uniqueness of monic division, with no cyclotomic commutator theorem used as a supplier. If $h_m\ge0$ the quotients have distinct leading degrees $h_m+k$ and unit leading coefficients $(-1)^r$, so $\rho$ is the displayed (transfer, dot-power unit) map from $F_iE_i\{-2d_i\}$ plus the $h_m$ identity columns to $E_iF_i$, and its inverse subtracts the section and inverts the transfer. If $h_m\le0$ the map $A$ is surjective with kernel $\mathrm{span}\{1,u,\dots,u^{-h_m-1}\}$, and the connecting images have an anti-triangular dot/cap matrix with unit anti-diagonal, whose successive solution gives the negative-branch inverse. This verifies the rank-one matrix and both inverse equations of the formal definition. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F3, algebra]

5.1 Same-color crossing, curl and bubble identities. Equal crossings act by $\kappa=(s-1)/(X-Y)$, so $\kappa^2=0$, the braid relation holds and the two mixed dot equations follow from the rational divided-difference expansion; $K_f$ is symmetric, so its divided-difference correction vanishes and $(X-Y)K_f=f(X)-f(Y)$ gives the dot-mate equations. Contracting a crossing against either Casimir and using the rank-one block inverse of step 4.1 produces the cross-and-cap/curl equations: expanding $(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the power bases and taking the top-coefficient rows gives the four signed sums over $a+b=-1$ and $a+b+c=-1$ with the stated orientation signs. The resulting oriented bubble Laurent series is $\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ of leading degree $h_m=N-2r$; its reciprocal is the opposite series with product $1$ coefficient by coefficient, forced by composing the two flag coefficient pairings, since each existing $i$ root contributes one factor from each side of the cap. Appending an $i$ root $z$ changes $\Phi_i$ to $\Phi_i/(u-z)^2$ and appending a spectator $j$ root $y$ changes it to $\Phi_iQ_{ij}(u,y)/t_{ij}$; expanding at infinity gives every finite bubble-slide coefficient equation. At a monic vacuum, $a_i(x)x^{\ell-1}=0$ gives $h_\ell+\sum_jc_{\lambda_i-j}h_{\ell-j}=0$ with $h_0=1$, $h_{<0}=0$, so $H(t)a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)=1$. All coefficients use only addition, multiplication and monic formal inversion. [step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Downward $Q$-relations and exact word grading. Give every flag the ordered shift $s_j(m)$ of the Statement. For $j<k$ the increasing word $(j,k)$ maps to the word $(k,j)$ by a quotient/switch of underlying degree $0$, with target-minus-source unit shift $-b_{jk}$; the reverse operator has underlying degree $-2b_{jk}$ and unit-shift $+b_{jk}$, so both have actual degree $-b_{jk}$, and same-color divided differences have degree $-2d_j$. Native operators are the negatives of the source operators, so their degrees and two-crossing composites are unchanged. The ordinary polynomial operators satisfy the idempotent, dot, far-commutation and quadratic $Q$-relations directly; expanding a three-strand composition gives zero difference for distinct outer colors and the divided difference of $Q$ for equal outer colors, and the global substitution $\kappa=-\tau$ changes all cubic signs to the native numerator. The quotient relations descend: on an $i,j$ pair $D_1$ has $bq=0$ and $D_0$ has $b=0$, and $Qb=t_{ij}bq$ makes multiplication by $Q$ well defined while the other crossing is the literal quotient. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, algebra]

6.2 Mixed cups and caps with their constants. In $D[z]/p$ versus $D[z]/(pq)$ the coefficient form satisfies $\tau_{pq}(Qf)=t_{ij}\tau_p(f)$, because $Q=t_{ij}q$ and the leading coefficient of $Qf$ is $t_{ij}$ times that of $f$. For a full existing $i$-string use the ordered residue form $t_r^p(z)=(-1)^{r(N-r)}\operatorname{Res}\bigl(\Delta_r(X)X_1^{r-1}\cdots X_{r-1}\operatorname{Tr}(z)/\prod_ap(X_a)\bigr)$, in which no $1/r!$ occurs; expanding parabolic divided differences verifies this over the universal integral coefficient ring, and over its generic-root fraction field the sum over root orderings is the Vandermonde determinant whose two factors cancel the internal root-difference denominator, so the identity is an integral polynomial identity and specializes to every field. With $p'=pq$ and $U_r=\prod_aQ_{ij}(X_a,y)$, cancellation gives $t_r^{p'}(U_rz)=(-1)^{rA_{ij}}t_{ij}^rt_r^p(z)$, and perfectness of the model forms makes $U_r$ injective on the old quotient. Testing the relative cap against these forms gives $\pi_r\varepsilon_r^{p'}(Q(X_{r+1},y)\operatorname{lift}(z))=(-1)^{A_{ij}}t_{ij}\varepsilon_r^p(z)$ for every nil-Hecke coset element. Normalizing the second maps by the global weight sign $(-1)^{h+1}$ — legitimate because $N$ and $h$ have the same parity and the new $N$ changes by $A_{ij}$ — cancels that sign and gives the exact constant $t_{ij}$; dual-power-basis contraction gives the mixed-unit equation, and reversing colors gives $t_{ji}$ with the stated double-mate ratio. Native minus signs occur twice in these composites, so the scalars persist. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Conclusion. Steps 3.1-6.2 verify every defining relation of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]] on the explicit flag modules: the generators and their degrees, both adjunction triangles, the rank-one matrices in both branches with their inverses, the bubble series and slides, the cross-and-cap equations, the mixed isomorphism with its scalars, and the downward $Q$-relations. Monic extensions, their Casimirs, the finite rank-one inverses and the coefficient identities survive arbitrary monic specialization as ungraded maps, and the construction is choice-free. This proves only the formal MODEL relations; faithfulness and the cyclotomic word-corner transfer belong to separate suppliers. [step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 6.2, discharge-construct: explicit flag modules] ∎

items.title: One-step simple restriction and induction, and the first-dot index
items.statement:
Let $k$ be any field and $R(Q)$ the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum and any homogeneous $Q$ satisfying the standing symmetry and
nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared
up to internal shift. For a simple $S$ of root weight $\beta$ and
$r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, its ordinary one-step last-$i$ restriction has a single
simple graded socle and a single simple graded head, each once and of the same
shift orbit, with $\epsilon_i=r-1$; its maximum-$\epsilon$ composition part has
coefficient a grading shift of $[r]_i$. The last-dot nilpotence index on that
restriction is exactly $r$. The first-end statements hold with
$\epsilon_i^L$ and the first dot. For every $n\ge1$,
$\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))$ has a unique simple graded head
$f_i^nS$, occurring once in its whole composition series, with
$\epsilon_i=r+n$ (also when $r=0$); all other constituents have smaller
$\epsilon_i$. One-step simple socle and simple induction head are partial
inverses. A simple $S$ survives the first-strand cyclotomic quotient with
exponents $\lambda_i$ exactly when $\epsilon_i^L(S)\le\lambda_i$ for all $i$.
Right restriction preserves surviving simples, while projected right induction
has the same simple head when that generic head survives and is zero
otherwise. These are shift-orbit assertions and do not assert factorial socle
multiplicity.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** compute the nil-Hecke branching explicitly, then use adjunction, the maximal-tail recursion and the shuffle bound to pin the socle, head and dot index of one-step restriction, and read off the induction head and the cyclotomic survival criterion.

1.1 Nil-Hecke branching. Put $z=t_r$ and write $E_a$ for the elementary symmetric polynomials in $t_1,\dots,t_{r-1}$. The relations $e_a=E_a+zE_{a-1}=0$ give $E_a=(-z)^a$ for $1\le a\le r-1$, and the top relation gives $z^r=0$; hence $C_r=k[t_1,\dots,t_{r-1}]\otimes_{k[E_1,\dots,E_{r-1}]}k[z]/(z^r)$ with $E_a$ acting by $(-z)^a$. The polynomial representation of $\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}$ is free of rank $(r-1)!$ over its symmetric center and identifies $\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}$ with the matrix algebra over that center; after the specialization its image on $C_r$ is $\mathrm{Mat}_{(r-1)!}(k[z]/(z^r))$ with standard column $C_r$. Therefore the graded socle and head of $C_r$ are each one shifted copy of the nil-Hecke simple, the simple composition coefficient is a shift of $[r]_i$, multiplication by $z$ has nilpotence index exactly $r$, the socle is the column over $z^{r-1}k$ and the head the column modulo $z$. For $r=1$ this reads $C_1=k$, $z=0$. The same computation with the first variable distinguished gives first-end branching, and matrix units plus a monic Artin basis make it valid in every characteristic. More generally, induction of $L(i^r)\boxtimes L(i^n)$ is killed by the positive symmetric center: each total elementary symmetric function restricts to a sum of products of the positive elementary functions in the two blocks. Its dimension is $\binom{r+n}{r}r!n!=(r+n)!$ by the shuffle basis. The augmentation quotient of $\mathrm{NH}_{r+n}$ is the full matrix algebra with simple column dimension $(r+n)!$, so this induced module is one shifted copy of $L(i^{r+n})$. [F1, F4, algebra]

1.2 Simple socle of one-step restriction. Let $S$ have $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$ and let $U\subseteq E_iS$ be a simple subobject with $t=\epsilon_i(U)$. The final dot $z$ commutes with $R(\beta-\alpha_i)$ and acts nilpotently on $E_iS$ (positive dot degree and finite graded support), preserving the socle and its ungraded isotypic components; on the isotypic component containing $U$ a nonzero power of $z$ has a nonzero kernel copy of the same simple type killed by $z$, and absolute simplicity and the finite graded semisimple decomposition let that copy be chosen homogeneously with the appropriate shift. Adjunction therefore produces a nonzero map $\operatorname{Ind}(U,L_1)\to S$, hence a surjection, and the shuffle bound [F4] gives $r\le t+1$ while the exact defining corners give $t\le r-1$; so $t=r-1$. [F1, F2, F4]

2.1 The maximal corner. Apply the maximal $(r-1)$-tail corner $p$ to $E_iS$, retaining $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)\otimes\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}$. By [F3], $\Delta_i^rS\cong N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$, so $p(E_iS)=N\boxtimes\operatorname{Res}_{\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}}L(i^r)$; by step 1.1 and the absolute simplicity of $N$ this has a single simple socle. Every simple subobject $U$ of $E_iS$ has $t=r-1$ by step 1.2, so [F3] makes $pU$ a nonzero simple object; exactness of $p$ makes $p(\operatorname{soc}E_iS)$ semisimple and injects it into the one-simple socle of $p(E_iS)$. Hence $\operatorname{soc}E_iS$ is a single simple object, once, with $\epsilon_i=r-1$; moreover every nonzero submodule of $E_iS$ contains a simple graded submodule whose $p$-image is nonzero (detection). [step 1.2, F3]

3.1 Simple head, detection and the dot index. Finite graded duality $D$ is exact, takes simples to simples, fixes corner idempotents and commutes with restriction, so applying step 2.1 to $DS$ (same $\epsilon_i$) and dualising gives a single simple head of $E_iS$, once; the maximal corner of its head is the head of $N\boxtimes\operatorname{Res}L(i^r)$, while the maximal corner of its socle is that tensor's socle. By step 1.1 these are shifts of the same $N\boxtimes L(i^{r-1})$. The unique-head recursion of [F3] therefore identifies their simple shift orbits. On $p(E_iS)$, step 1.1 gives $z^r=0$ and $z^{r-1}\ne0$; the image of $z^r$ on all of $E_iS$ is a graded submodule with zero $p$-corner, so detection in step 2.1 forces it to be zero, while nonvanishing of $z^{r-1}$ in the corner forces it to be nonzero globally. Hence the last-dot nilpotence index on $E_iS$ is exactly $r$; repeating with the first variable gives first-dot index exactly $\epsilon_i^L(S)$. [step 2.1, F1, F2]

4.1 Nonreduced induction and its unique head. Put $M_n=\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))$, $n\ge1$. Its maximum tail is at most $r+n$ by the shuffle bound; at tail $r+n$ the Mackey filtration retains exactly all $n$ added $i$-strands together with $r$ terminal $i$-strands of $S$, its surviving corner is $N\boxtimes\operatorname{Ind}_{\mathrm{NH}_r\otimes\mathrm{NH}_n}^{\mathrm{NH}_{r+n}}(L(i^r)\boxtimes L(i^n))$. The final computation of step 1.1 makes this $N\boxtimes L(i^{r+n})$ up to the fixed shift. Every simple quotient $T$ of $M_n$ has that maximum tail: adjunction gives a nonzero injection $S\boxtimes L(i^n)\hookrightarrow\Delta_i^nT$, and restricting the first factor to the maximal $r$-tail retains a nonzero corner of $T$'s maximal corner, so $\epsilon_i(T)\ge r+n$, and the shuffle bound gives equality. Hence the finite semisimple head of $M_n$ has only constituents detected by its simple maximal corner, so it is one simple constituent, once; the kernel of $M_n\to\operatorname{hd}M_n$ has zero maximal corner, so every other composition factor has smaller $\epsilon_i$ and the head occurs exactly once in the whole composition series. Write $f_iS:=\operatorname{hd}M_1$. [step 1.1, step 3.1, F3, F4]

5.1 Partial inverses, iterates and the cyclotomic criterion. Adjunction realises $S$ in $E_i(f_iS)$, so step 2.1 gives $\operatorname{soc}E_if_iS=S$ with shifts restored; conversely $S=\operatorname{soc}E_iT$ implies $T$ is a simple quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}(S,L_1)$, hence $T=f_iS$. Thus one-step socle and head are partial inverses, $f_i$ raises $\epsilon_i$ by one and $\operatorname{soc}E_i$ lowers it by one; iterating the one-strand argument gives $\operatorname{hd}\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))=f_i^nS$. Let $J^\Lambda$ be generated by $x_1^{\lambda_i}$ on every word beginning with $i$; it annihilates a simple $S$ exactly when each first-$i$ corner has first-dot index at most $\lambda_i$, which by step 3.1 is $\epsilon_i^L(S)$, so $J^\Lambda S=0$ iff $\epsilon_i^L(S)\le\lambda_i$ for every $i$; if a generator is nonzero, simplicity forces $J^\Lambda S=S$. Right restriction preserves first strands, hence the cyclotomic subcategory; for induction, the generic unique head either survives, in which case the quotient induction has the same head, or dies, in which case the quotient induction is zero because every nonzero finite module has a simple quotient. The maximal-$\epsilon$ composition part is the same simple shift orbit as the head and socle, with coefficient a shift of $[r]_i$ by step 1.1. No choice and no self-dual representative is used. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F1, F2] ∎

items.title: PBW and bubble normal form in the minimal-parabolic diagram category
items.statement: Fix a color $i$. In the formal graded minimal-parabolic proof category of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], the reduced perfect-matching diagrams, dot monomials on their open components, and monomials in the independent far-left normalized $i$-bubble coefficients form a basis of every morphism space. In particular, at all-downward boundaries of weight difference $\beta$, the morphism space is the corresponding KLR PBW corner tensored with the polynomial ring in one positive bubble family; the opposite/fake family is its coefficientwise reciprocal. The graded polynomial flag models of [[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]], with universal monic framing and arbitrarily large auxiliary framing at each fixed physical source weight, are jointly faithful. The assertion is about this formal proof category before cyclotomic quotient transfer.
items.strategy:
Use $\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for all colors. The formal category's relations are the exact model-verified local equations: downward KLR, both rank-one triangles, cyclic dots, rho/cross-and-cap equations and bubble inversion, mixed cap/cup equations, and the finite-coefficient bubble slides. For an $i$ root $x$, its normalized bubble series changes by $(1-xt)^{\pm2}$; for a spectator $j$ root $y$ it changes by $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)^{\pm1}$, where $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$ has constant coefficient $1$. These are verified directly because the model series is $p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2$, adjoining an $i$ root multiplies $c_r$ by $u-x$, and adjoining a spectator multiplies $p$ by $Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$. Every fixed inverse coefficient is a finite polynomial recursion. These slides are specified formal relations checked on the model; deriving a slide from the faithfulness being proved is not used.

To span, move dots to fixed component positions with cyclicity and KLR dot moves. An equal-color correction has one fewer crossing. Sort each $i$ cup/cap toward a boundary or the far-left closed-component position using the specified mate equations. A main term passes one of its finitely many crossing obstacles; a correction term removes an unsorted open-component extremum or such an obstacle. Rank-one cross-and-cap sums are finite: open dot counts are nonnegative and negative-degree bubbles vanish, bounding the indices at a fixed total degree. Adjacent opposed cup/cap pairs cancel by the triangles. Induct on the lexicographic pair of unsorted extrema and remaining crossing obstacles, and on crossing length for correction terms. Closed components have color $i$; cancel extra extrema, slide them left by the finite coefficient equations, and express the reverse family by bubble inversion. Coxeter deletion and KLR braid/quadratic straightening then reduce each open matching to the selected reduced diagram, with all braid defects shorter. This yields the stated finite span. At all-downward boundaries every open arc joins bottom to top, hence is a colored permutation; the reduced matching and its dots are exactly a PBW monomial. For general boundaries the two triangles give invertible Hom correspondences bending the upward $i$ endpoints to the other boundary, and the same straightening has unit leading matching coefficients.

For independence hold the physical source weight $\mu$ fixed and write $\mu_i=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$. Choose fixed nonnegative spectator background counts $m_j$ and let $A_{\rm spect}=\sum_{j\ne i}(-a_{ij})m_j$. For an increasing background $i$ count $r$, set $N=\mu_i+2r$ and $\lambda_i=N-A_{\rm spect}$. These equations keep the physical weight $N-2r=\mu_i$ fixed. Only $i$ dominance is needed, since the model has no spectator upward generator; one may take all $m_j=0$. Use the universal graded monic framing $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}+z_1u^{\lambda_i-1}+\cdots+z_{\lambda_i}$ with independent $\deg z_a=2d_i a$. Put $p=a_i\prod Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $c_r=\prod(u-x_a)$. The correct normalized series is $\mathcal B(t)=p^{\rm rev}/(c_r^{\rm rev})^2=a_i^{\rm rev}U(t)$, $U_0=1$. Its coefficient $\mathcal B_a=z_a+\sum_{1\le\ell<a}z_\ell U_{a-\ell}+U_a$ is unit triangular in the framing variables. The reciprocal family's coefficient is $-z_a$ plus lower framing indices. Thus the first $D$ bubble coefficients are independent whenever $\lambda_i\ge D$, even in characteristic two and at negative physical weight. No claim of a unit old-root coefficient is made: $\mathcal B_1=p_1+2e_1$ can lose its root term in characteristic two.

A nonzero finite PBW/bubble combination remains nonzero after that triangular substitution over the independent polynomial coefficient domain. The generic KLR polynomial representation has a distinct nonzero leading permutation for each selected crossing word; choose a polynomial test vector with nonzero output, clearing a finite denominator if needed. Let $D$ bound the bubble indices and let $B$ bound the actual internal degrees of that vector and its output; both are finite and are determined in the untruncated polynomial ring. Let $L$ bound the number of added $i$ flags in the tested words. Every monic flag relation and factor-ring coefficient relation after those flags has degree at least $2d_i(N-r-L+1)=2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)$; spectator appends can only increase $N$. All coefficient and root variables are nonnegatively graded and all dot degrees are positive. Choose $r\ge0$, $\lambda_i\ge D$, and $2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)>B$, also making any finitely required background root count large enough. Such an integer exists while $\mu$ is fixed. The ideal generated by the homogeneous model relations cannot meet degrees at most $B$, so the nonzero PBW output survives in that flag model. This is exact degree separation, not a deformation-flatness inference. The model's ordered word shifts, $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$ with $i$ last, make every crossing homogeneous of degree $-b_{jk}$; the polynomial witness is checked before its overall word shift. The formal upward generator is $H_i=E_i^{\rm basic}\{-d_i(1+h_{\rm input})\}$, not unnormalized restriction, so its spectator commutators are truly degree zero. Hence the faithful underlying witness is also a witness in the specified graded model.

The downward spanning map is therefore injective. The finite unit-triangular bending change then gives independence for the full matching family. Specializing the far-left bubble variables acts only on that tensor factor in the downward normal form; no ordinary KLR relation appears from coefficient evaluation alone. Universal grading is used only to witness formal faithfulness; subsequent inhomogeneous monic field specialization is governed by the separately proved algebraic cap-off kernel.

items.title: Cyclotomic induction is projective on the right
items.statement:
Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], and let
$E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]. For every $i\in I$
and $\beta\in Q_+$:

(a) the bimodule $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i)$ is a projective right
$R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module, and $e(\beta,i)R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ is a
projective left $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module;

(b) consequently $E^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_i$ are exact and send finitely
generated graded projectives to finitely generated graded projectives;
moreover $F^\Lambda_i$ preserves all projectives and $E^\Lambda_i$ preserves
finitely generated ones;

(c) there is a functorial exact sequence in
$\mathrm{Mod}(R(\beta+\alpha_i))$
$$0\longrightarrow q^{(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)}\bar F_iM\longrightarrow F_iM\longrightarrow F^\Lambda_iM\longrightarrow 0,\qquad M\in\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta)),$$
where $F_i$ is the right-append and $\bar F_i$ the left-append generic
induction of
[[lem-generic-klr-induction-and-restriction-mixed-relations]], regarded on
$R^\Lambda$-modules through the quotient, and the exponent is the Cartan
pairing $(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)=2(\alpha_i\mid\Lambda)
-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] records the
normalization of the powers of $q$).

**Proof technique:** compare the cyclotomic towers over the generic ones with an explicit monic comparison map, then use the monic-annihilator projective splitting to deduce projectivity, exactness and the exact sequence with its shift.

If $A=0$, the comparison modules and functor values are zero, so all assertions are vacuous; polynomial degrees below are used only for $A
e0$.

1.1 Comparison modules and their projectivity. Put $n=| eta|$ and let $R_1( eta)=\xi_nR( eta)$ act on positions $2,\ldots,n+1$. For $n>0$ set $J_0=Sa(x_1)R( eta)e_R$ and $J_1=Sa(x_2)R_1( eta)e_L$; for $n=0$ set $J_0=J_1=0$, since the old block has no cyclotomic relation. Put $K_0=Se_R/J_0$, $K_1=Se_L/J_1$. The right action of $A[t]$ on $K_0$ uses the first $n$ strands and $t=x_{n+1}$; on $K_1$ it uses $\xi_n$ and $t=x_1$. The labelled PBW cosets make $Se_R$ and $Se_L$ finite projective over the corresponding separated-block algebras $R( eta)[t]$: each homogeneous coset summand is a shifted principal word-idempotent module. Tensoring these summands with $A[t]$ gives precisely $K_0,K_1$, so both are finite projective over $A[t]$. At $n=0$ both are $k[t]$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 Monic annihilators and projectivity, locally. Let $0	o P_1\xrightarrow{j}P_0	o M	o0$ be an exact sequence of right $A[t]$-modules with finite projective $P_0,P_1$, and suppose a central monic $f$ annihilates $M$. Multiplication by $f$ is injective on a free $A[t]$-module by its unit leading coefficient, hence on its projective summands. On a finite free module monic division gives an $A$-linear operator $p_{\mathrm{free}}$ taking a polynomial to its quotient by $f$, with $p_{\mathrm{free}}(xf)=x$. Choose split inclusion $u:P_1	o A[t]^N$ and projection $v:A[t]^N	o P_1$; then $p=vp_{\mathrm{free}}u$ satisfies $p(xf)=x$ on $P_1$, since $u$ is $A[t]$-linear and $vu=1$. Since $fM=0$, multiplication by $f$ on $P_0$ has image in $j(P_1)$, defining $h:P_0	o P_1$ by $jh=f$. Injectivity of $j$ gives $hj=f$ on $P_1$, so $phj=1$. Thus $j$ has the $A$-linear retraction $ph$, and $M$ is a direct summand of the $A$-projective module $P_0$ and is $A$-projective. Equivalently, $P_r/fP_r$ is a summand of $(A[t]/fA[t])^N\cong A^{mN}$ and is $A$-projective, which is the monic-quotient reason for the splitting. This argument uses finite projective presentations and division and does not assume $f$ invertible or the target $M$ projective. [F3, algebra]

2.1 The cyclotomic ideal and the map $P$. Throughout put $\kappa_a=-	au_a$. The first-position PBW cosets give $S=\sum_{r=0}^n(k^I[x_1]\otimes R_1(n))\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_r$. Since $a(x_1)$ commutes with this coefficient algebra, $Sa(x_1)S=\sum_{r=0}^nSa(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_r$. After multiplying by $e_R$, terms $r<n$ lie in $J_0$; the remaining term is the image of $\widetilde P:Se_L	o K_0$, $u\mapsto ua(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_n$. Thus its image is the kernel of $K_0	o Be_R$, where $B=R^\Lambda( eta+\alpha_i)$. To check right linearity, move $x_{a+1}$ through $a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_n$ to $x_a$ and move $x_1$ to $x_{n+1}$. Each mixed-relation correction omits one transfer crossing and has the form, up to its color projector and sign, $(\kappa_{a+1}\cdots\kappa_n)a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_{a-1}$, hence belongs to $J_0$. Moving $\kappa_{a+1}$ to $\kappa_a$ introduces only the braid correction $a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_{a-1}D_a\kappa_{a+2}\cdots\kappa_n$, with $D_a$ a dot polynomial; the far crossings can be moved left and the last-dot powers commute with the shorter word, again putting it in $J_0$. Idempotents follow the cyclic transfer. These generator identities prove $\widetilde P$ is right $R( eta)[t]$-linear. It therefore kills $J_1$, and induces an $(S,A[t])$-map $P:K_1	o K_0$ with the same image. [step 1.1, F1, algebra]

3.1 Intertwiners and the map $Q$. Define $g_a=\kappa_a$ on unequal adjacent colors and $g_a=(x_{a+1}-x_a)-(x_{a+1}-x_a)^2\kappa_a$ on equal colors. The source mixed relations give $x_{s_a(b)}g_a=g_ax_b$ for every $b$. They also give $\kappa_ag_{a+1}g_a=g_{a+1}g_a\kappa_{a+1}$: subtract the two sides and use the mixed relations to see that the difference intertwines $x_a$ with $x_{a+2}$ and fixes $x_{a+1}$. In the faithful localized polynomial realization [F4], its longest-permutation coefficients cancel, since both products cross the same three color pairs with the same factors. All remaining permutations have length at most two, and none interchanges $a$ and $a+2$ while fixing the middle variable. Independence of the permutation operators then forces every coefficient to vanish. Consequently right multiplication by $g_n\cdots g_1$ intertwines old dots/crossings with their shifted copies and $x_{n+1}$ with $x_1$. It descends to $Q:K_0	o K_1$: the first-position cosets write $J_0$ as the sum of the terms $Sa(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_r e_R$, $r<n$, and the intertwining identities send each such term to $Sg_n\cdots g_1a(x_2)\kappa_2\cdots\kappa_{r+1}e_L\subseteq J_1$. items.title: The cyclotomic cap-off quotient has no extra downward relations
items.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be dominant, $\lambda_j=\langle h_j,\Lambda\rangle$, and let $\mathcal P_i$ be [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], with its homogeneous polynomial realization and PBW/bubble normal form. Fix monic $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}+\sum_{r<\lambda_j}c_{j,r}u^r$. For the standard graded cyclotomic quotient take $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$ as in [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]. More generally first take universal graded coefficients of degree $2d_j(\lambda_j-r)$; arbitrary monic specializations over the field are interpreted as ungraded.

In the representable category $\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)$, let $J$ be the ideal generated by $1_{H_iv_\Lambda}$ and $a_j(x)1_{G_jv_\Lambda}$ for every $j$, closed under arbitrary vertical pre/postcomposition and horizontal whiskering by the allowed 1-morphisms. For downward words $\mu,\nu$ of the same weight $\beta$, include their ordinary KLR corner by the PBW/bubble normal form. Then
$$J\cap e(\nu)R(\beta)e(\mu)=e(\nu)I_a(\beta)e(\mu),\qquad I_a(\beta)=\sum_j R(\beta)a_j(x_1)e(j,\beta-\alpha_j)R(\beta).$$

These are mathematical suppliers, not a citation-only import. Apply the following finite argument before transporting any formal relation to the actual cyclotomic action.

## Vacuum coefficients: the specialization is forced, not an extra assumption

Use the trace packet's normalized cups/caps; let h_l be the bubble closed with lambda_i-1+l dots and extend negative-dot symbols by formal inversion. The formal rank-one identities give h_l=0 for l<0 and h_0=1. Close a_i(x)x^{l-1}=0 for l>=1. The exponent l-1 is nonnegative, so this is a lawful defining-ideal consequence, including when some resulting indices are negative. It gives

$$h_l+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}h_{l-1}+\cdots+c_{i,0}h_{l-\lambda_i}=0.$$

Thus H(t)=sum_{l>=0} h_l t^l is the inverse of a_i^{rev}(t)=1+c_{i,lambda_i-1}t+...+c_{i,0}t^{lambda_i}. Bubble inversion determines the opposite family A(t)=H(t)^{-1}=a_i^{rev}(t). Consequently Phi_i(u)=u^{lambda_i}A(u^{-1})=a_i(u). Each coefficient conclusion uses only a finite recurrence. The local polynomial-model supplier proves these rank-one identities; no faithful cyclotomic action or generic Frobenius theorem is used.

Distinguish the index from the literal dot count. An actual vacancy loop with r>=0 dots has A index lambda_i+1+r; it vanishes because A is a polynomial of degree at most lambda_i. The A coefficients with index 1,...,lambda_i are fake bubbles of negative dot count; in the monic branch they are prescribed coefficients, not zero. The opposite H family is generally an infinite reciprocal series. For a_i=u(u-1), A=1-t and H=(1-t)^{-1}. Setting all positive bubbles in both orientations to zero would wrongly change this deformation. In the standard branch both positive coefficient families vanish. If lambda_i=0, a_i=1 kills F_i v and A=H=1; the degree-zero fake coefficient remains 1.

Write S for this vacuum bubble coefficient specialization. By the recurrence S is already contained in J. By [[lem-minimal-parabolic-diagrams-have-pbw-bubble-normal-form]], specializing these central vacuum coefficients alone gives the all-downward corner R(beta), with no relations in its ordinary polynomial/crossing part. This uses the tensor-product normal form, not a flatness assertion. We can calculate in P_i/S and then include the E_i and first-strand generators.

## Bringing every bubble coefficient to the vacuum

After bending, a coefficient may initially be a bubble at source Lambda+alpha_i, immediately to the left of an added first i strand with dot z. It may not be replaced directly by the Lambda vacuum value. The required rank-one bubble-slide equation in coefficient normalization is

$$A_{\Lambda+\alpha_i}(t)=(1-zt)^2A_\Lambda(t),\qquad H_{\Lambda+\alpha_i}(t)=(1-zt)^{-2}H_\Lambda(t).$$

The weight indices differ by 2; these are normalized power series with constant coefficient 1. For each fixed coefficient this is a finite polynomial equation in z and the vacuum coefficients. Negative exponents on (1-zt) denote formal coefficient recursion, not inversion of z or an analytic infinite sum.

Here is an algebraic verification, independent of quotient faithfulness. In the unquotiented rank-one polynomial flag model, with total monic polynomial p and existing-root factor c_r, the normalized bubble series is p^{rev}/(c_r^{rev})^2; this is the coefficient/cap identity for the two monic flag pairings (equivalently complement factor divided by root factor). Adding the distinguished root z replaces c_r^{rev} by c_r^{rev}(1-zt). The target series is therefore the source series divided by (1-zt)^2. Multiplying proves the displayed equation; inversion gives the H equation. These finite coefficient equalities are explicit relations in the definition of the formal proof category and are verified by the local polynomial-model supplier. They are not derived from the normal-form faithfulness theorem that subsequently uses them for spanning. This uses only monic polynomial multiplication and coefficient inversion before quotienting, and does not claim that faithfulness survives a quotient.

Thus a finite diagram has, after finitely many coefficient slides, only polynomial dots on the added strand and bubble coefficients at Lambda. In P_i/S these coefficients are scalars. No source-weight bubble specialization or collision of two distinguished roots is assumed.

## The actual local straight and curl calculations

Use the actual rank-one cross-and-cap equations and their finite polynomial verification in the local model supplier; the same equations appear in Webster Figure2. The following dot-index calculation types the contraction directly and requires no two-root-collision identification.

The straight closure of the added leftmost i strand with r dots is the actual vacancy loop, with A index lambda_i+1+r. It is zero in P_i/S. This remains true for any polynomial dots with coefficients on the neighboring original strand, by linearity and dot cyclicity.

For the leftward single-crossing curl, Figure 2 expands it as a signed sum of a dotted uncrossed cap and a far-left bubble, with dot indices a+b=-1 and a>=0. Put b=-lambda_i-1+m. The bubble coefficient is A_m, and a=lambda_i-m. Terms with m<0 have negative bubble degree and vanish; terms with m>lambda_i have negative dots on the open strand and vanish. Therefore the undotted local curl is

$$\epsilon\sum_{m=0}^{\lambda_i}A_m x^{\lambda_i-m}=\epsilon a_i(x),\qquad \epsilon\in\{1,-1\}.$$

The sign is the fixed orientation/source-crossing unit. Since the statement is ideal membership, its value is immaterial; no unsigned equality of canonical maps is claimed. In characteristic 2 it is still a unit. When lambda_i=0 the sum is epsilon times the identity, matching a_i=1.

For f in the included downward R corner belonging to J, express f as a finite sum of vertically factored horizontal whiskers of the defining generators. Add S, which was already forced by J. The forward inclusion follows directly from the initial a_j generators and downward whiskering/vertical composition. items.title: The two-colour jump formula and strict elementary embeddings
items.statement:
Let $k$ be any field and $R(Q)$ the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum and any homogeneous $Q$ satisfying the standing symmetry and
nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared up
to internal shift. Set $c_i(S)=\epsilon_i^L(S)$ and
$J_i(S)=\max\{n\ge0:c_i(f_i^nS)=c_i(S)\}$. This maximum is finite and
$J_i(S)=\epsilon_i(S)+c_i(S)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$ for
$S$ of root weight $\beta\in Q_+$. For $i\ne j$ one has $c_i(f_jS)=c_i(S)$; for
$j=i$ it stays constant or increases by $1$, and increase is equivalent to
$f_iS=f_i^LS$ and to simplicity of $\operatorname{Ind}(S,L(i))$. Once it
increases, it increases at every later right-$i$ step. Put
$\operatorname{wt}(S)=-\beta$ and $\phi_i=\epsilon_i+\langle h_i,
\operatorname{wt}\rangle$. The maps
$\Psi_i(S)=(e_i^L)^{c_i(S)}S\otimes b_i(-c_i(S))$ are strict injective
elementary-crystal maps, and every nonvacuum simple has positive extraction at
some $i$. The simple graph is lowering-generated with every generic $f_i$
nonzero. In any first-strand cyclotomic quotient containing $S$ the actual
surviving lowering length is
$\lambda_i+\epsilon_i(S)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$. All containing-weight
arguments take place in the auxiliary primitive-coroot finite-support datum,
leaving $R,A,D,Q$ unchanged, so no positive-dominant-label assumption on the
original $P$ is added. Linear divided restriction/$G_0$ operators satisfy the
quantum Serre relation; the simple-socle crystal operators are not asserted to
satisfy a linear Serre identity.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** reduce all weight comparisons to a finite support, use the one-step socle/head calculus with the shuffle bound to prove the jump lemma, then read off the jump index, the strict embeddings and the cyclotomic surviving length.

1.1 Finite reduction and two elementary tools. Restrict every containing-weight argument to the finite colour support of the modules and the finitely many selected strings by [F2]; all bounds and coordinates are then finite and the algebras, Cartan data and parameters are unchanged. For an exact induction functor: if $\operatorname{Ind}(A,H)\to T$ is surjective with $T$ simple, choose the first term of a composition series whose induced image is nonzero; that image is $T$ and the previous term maps to zero, giving a surjection $\operatorname{Ind}(A,U)\to T$ from some simple composition factor $U$. If $\epsilon_i(A)=0$ and $\operatorname{Ind}(A,U)\to T$ is nonzero with $U,T$ simple, then $\epsilon_i(T)=\epsilon_i(U)$: the shuffle bound gives $\epsilon_i(T)\le\epsilon_i(U)$, and adjunction injects $A\otimes U$ into the restriction of $T$, whose terminal $\epsilon_i(U)$ corner is nonzero, giving the reverse inequality. [F2, algebra]

2.1 The jump lemma. Adjunction for $\operatorname{Ind}(M,L(j))\to f_jM$ together with the shuffle bound gives $c_i(M)\le c_i(f_jM)\le c_i(M)+\delta_{ij}$. For $i\ne j$ this is equality, and first-end symmetry gives $\epsilon_i(f_j^LM)=\epsilon_i(M)$. Suppose $c_i(f_iM)=c_i(M)+1$: the reversed induction $\operatorname{Ind}(L(i),M)$ has the same ungraded character as $\operatorname{Ind}(M,L(i))$, hence the same ungraded composition factors, and its unique maximal-first-tail factor is $f_i^LM$ once, so $f_iM=f_i^LM$; conversely this equality forces the increase. Since finite duality commutes with $e_i,f_i$ on shift orbits, $\operatorname{coInd}(M,L_n)$ has simple socle $f_i^nM$, and the positive-shift coinduction formula gives $\operatorname{soc}\operatorname{Ind}(M,L_n)=(f_i^L)^nM$ and $\operatorname{soc}\operatorname{Ind}(L_n,M)=f_i^nM$ on shift orbits. [step 1.1, F1, F3]

3.1 Increase persists; the jump index. If $f_iM=f_i^LM$ then the same simple is head and socle of $\operatorname{Ind}(M,L_1)$, occurring once in the whole composition series by [F1]; a finite-length module with a simple socle equal to its head occurring once is simple (otherwise the socle lies in the radical and gives a second occurrence of the head). Hence $\operatorname{Ind}(M,L_1)$ is simple and equals $\operatorname{Ind}(L_1,M)$, and iterating gives $\operatorname{Ind}(M,L_n)=\operatorname{Ind}(L_n,M)$ up to shift, with simple unique head and socle for every $n$; in particular $c_i(f_i^nM)=c_i(M)+n$ for all $n$, so once $c_i$ increases it increases at every later right-$i$ step. Set $J_i(M)=\max\{n:c_i(f_i^nM)=c_i(M)\}$; the separate root-height induction with the two-colour growth and the annihilation lemma bounds it without presuming integrability in an unbounded $i$-direction, and once finite the zero-jump lemma gives $J_i(f_iM)=\max(0,J_i(M)-1)$. Combining with the one-step formula $c_i(f_iM)=c_i(M)+[f_iM=f_i^LM]$ yields $J_i(S)=\epsilon_i(S)+c_i(S)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$ for $S$ of root weight $\beta$, the claimed formula. [step 2.1, F1]

4.1 Strict elementary embeddings. With $\operatorname{wt}(S)=-\beta$ and $\phi_i=\epsilon_i+\langle h_i,\operatorname{wt}\rangle$, the one-step socle/head identities make $\Psi_i(S)=(e_i^L)^{c_i(S)}S\otimes b_i(-c_i(S))$ a strict injective elementary-crystal map: extraction increases by $c_i(S)$ on the image and the weight is shifted by $-c_i(S)\alpha_i$, and the assignment is injective on simple shift orbits by the uniqueness of the socle in [F1]. Every nonvacuum simple has positive extraction at some colour, since otherwise each $\epsilon_i^L$ vanishes and the module would be a vacuum; the simple graph is lowering-generated because every generic $f_i$ is nonzero by [F1] and $e_i$ recovers the source on shift orbits. [step 3.1, F1]

5.1 The cyclotomic surviving length and Serre. In any first-strand cyclotomic quotient containing $S$, the relation $x_1^{\lambda_i}$ kills precisely when the first-dot index $\epsilon_i^L(S)$ is at most $\lambda_i$; reading the formula of step 3.1 at the level of $G_0$ gives the actual surviving lowering length $\lambda_i+\epsilon_i(S)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$ for the right operator, and the same count at the first end by symmetry. The linear divided restriction operators on $G_0$ satisfy the quantum Serre relation by [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]]; the simple-socle operators $e_i,f_i$ themselves are not claimed to satisfy a linear Serre identity. No positive-dominant label assumption on the original $P$ is made, since every weight comparison took place in the auxiliary finite-support datum of [F2]. [step 3.1, step 4.1, F2] ∎

items.statement:
Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], let
$E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]], and read the
composites $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i$ as
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$ via the weight bookkeeping
fixed there. Put $\lambda:=\Lambda-\beta$ and $q_i:=q^{d_i}$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

(a) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\ge0$, there is a natural isomorphism of
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{2k}\mathrm{Id}\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i.$$

(b) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\le0$, there is a natural isomorphism of
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{-\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{-2k-2}\mathrm{Id}.$$

Applied to the object $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ the same computation gives an
isomorphism of graded $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-bimodules obtained from
$F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ and
$E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ by the displayed summands
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]] for the shift
conventions).
