items.title: Coherent graded biadjunction and the crossing mates
items.statement:
For the standard homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient over any field and every homogeneous Q1–Q4 datum, use basic right-append induction $F_i$ from $ eta$ to $ eta+\alpha_i$ and basic restriction $E_i$ in the reverse direction. Put $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda- etaangle$ and $t_i( eta)=2d_i(1-h)=(\alpha_i|\alpha_i)-2(\Lambda- eta|\alpha_i)$. There are explicit homogeneous bimodule units and counits with both triangle identities giving $E_i\{t_i( eta)\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ on all graded module categories. They preserve the standard dot-cyclic and same-color crossing-mate identities and the coherent different-color double-mate identity: for $p_
u=	au_r e(
u)$ with bottom adjacent colors $(i,j)$, $i
e j$, its double right mate is $(t_{ji}/t_{ij})p_
u$, where $t_{ij}$ is the coefficient of $u^{-a_{ij}}$ in $Q_{ij}(u,v)$ and the strand of color $i$ runs SW to NE. Equivalently the associated right closure satisfies $\operatorname{cl}(p_
u a)=(t_{ji}/t_{ij})\operatorname{cl}(a p_
u)$ for $a\in e(
u)R^\Lambda( eta)e(s_r
u)$; dots, idempotents and equal-color crossings have ratio $1$. The corresponding arbitrary monic field quotients have the same underlying ungraded biadjunction and ordered crossing-mate identities after forgetting internal shifts. No Frobenius, integral Grothendieck-module or crystal theorem is a premise.
items.strategy:
Work throughout with $\kappa=-\tau_{\rm native}$ for every color pair. This is a graded algebra isomorphism preserving $Q$ and all first-strand monic ideals: quadratic relations have two signs, the braid defect three, and $\kappa_w=(-1)^{\ell(w)}\tau_w$. Hence model crossings are native $-\pi$ and $-Q$; changing only equal-color crossings is not allowed. Use the formal category and its explicit graded flag model from the declared suppliers. With $i$ last in a total color order, raw downward flags have shifts $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$. A degree-$D$ raw map between word shifts $S,T$ has degree $D+T-S$. Thus a source increasing crossing $\pi$ of degree zero and its reverse multiplier $Q$ of degree $-2b_{jk}$ both have actual degree $-b_{jk}$. Basic $E_iG_j$ has the prescribed $-b_{ij}$ shifted commutation. Formal $H_i=E_i^{\rm basic}\{-d_i(1+h_{\rm input})\}$ cancels that shift: $h$ increases by $-a_{ij}$ under $G_j$ and $s_j(m-e_i)=s_j(m)+b_{ij}$. It is formal $H_i$, rather than basic $E_i$, that commutes unshiftedly with the spectator flag.

At a vertex with $r$ i roots and total monic degree $N$, put $L=C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]/(\text{factor coefficients above }N-r)$, $c_r=\prod(u-x_a)$, $p=a_i\prod Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $b=p/c_r$. The i-flag algebra is $B=L[z]/b(z)$, free over the old ring on powers $0\le j<N-r$ and free over the target root-append ring on powers $0\le j\le r$. The two coefficient traces $\tau_{\rm old}$ and $\tau_{\rm new}$ extract the respective top powers in their monic remainders. Their Gram matrices in power/complementary bases are triangular with diagonal one, so they have explicit dual bases without factorial denominators. Basic $F_i=B\{-2d_i r\}\otimes-$ and basic reverse $E_i=B\otimes-$ use $\tau_{\rm new}$ and its dual bases for the first adjunction and $\tau_{\rm old}$ for the second. If $(u_a,v_a)$ are either pair of dual bases, the unit is $1\mapsto\sum_av_a\otimes u_a$ and the counit is its coefficient trace. The identities $\sum_av_a\tau(u_ax)=x$ and $\sum_a\tau(xv_a)u_a=x$ give both triangles directly. The trace-degree difference is $-2d_i(N-2r-1)=t_i(\beta)$. Source second maps are normalized by $(-1)^{N+1}=(-1)^{h+1}$, with the unit given the inverse scalar; degree-zero bubbles are one. Transporting $\kappa=-\tau$ preserves these maps and triangles, and dots/crossings inherit their actual pairing-adjoint identities.

For coherent mixed maps, let $Q_{ij}(u,y)=t_{ij}q(u,y)$ with $q$ monic and replace $p$ by $pq$. The successive i/j flags have rings modulo $b$ and $bq$; their source crossings are quotient $\pi$ and multiplication by $Q$. Monic coefficient extraction gives $\epsilon_{pq}(Qf)=t_{ij}\epsilon_p(f)$ on the one-variable power basis. On all nil-Hecke matrix entries use the ordered residue form $t_r^p(z)=(-1)^{r(N-r)}\operatorname{Res}(\Delta_r b_r\operatorname{Tr}(z)/\prod_s p(X_s))$, with $\Delta_r=\prod_{s<t}(X_s-X_t)$ and $b_r=X_1^{r-1}\cdots X_{r-1}$. It equals the integral parabolic divided-difference form: summing ordered distinct roots gives $\Delta^2$, repeated roots vanish, and the resulting integral polynomial identity specializes to every characteristic. There is no $1/r!$. For $U_r=\prod_sQ_{ij}(X_s,y)$, cancellation gives $t_r^{pq}(U_rz)=(-1)^{r(-a_{ij})}t_{ij}^r t_r^p(z)$. Perfect coefficient pairings then give the full relative identity $\pi_r\widehat\epsilon^{pq}(Q(X_{r+1},y)\operatorname{lift}z)=t_{ij}\widehat\epsilon^p(z)$ after the global second-map normalization; it holds for every matrix/coset element. Its ordinary mate is the mixed-unit identity. Native single crossings add one minus sign, while the two-sideways composites have two and retain $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$. Their ordered quotient is $t_{ji}/t_{ij}$ for the i strand running SW–NE. This proves the formal crossing-mate relation without assuming a one-dimensional Hom space.

Transfer that formal relation to the actual first-strand quotient using the declared cap-off kernel supplier and PBW/bubble normal form, not rank-one detection of arbitrary map equality. Let $J$ be generated by $H_iv_\Lambda$ and $a_j(x)G_jv_\Lambda$. The marked i generator closed with dot powers forces $H(t)a_i^{\rm rev}(t)=1$; its canonical unit columns $x^k\eta$, $k<\lambda_i$, have companion polynomial exactly $a_i$. Genuine vacancy loops have index $\lambda_i+1+s$ and vanish, whereas the lower fake coefficients in the monic branch are retained. Every factor through a vacuum $H_i$ bends to an added first i strand. The cap-off supplier proves the full two-double-coset PBW reduction: no first crossing closes to that zero loop; one first crossing must be equal-color and its actual cross-and-cap sum is a unit sign times $a_i(x)$, with decorated value $a_i(x)P(x,x)$. Physical exterior factors commute with closure. Arbitrary upward whiskers of a marked $a_j$ reduce by input naturality of the mixed maps/rho; for negative h use the actual retract $\iota=\rho^{-1}j_{EF}$, $\pi=p_{EF}\rho$, $\pi\iota=1$. The branch reaching the marker is zero by the companion matrix when j=i or by mixed dot commutation and $H_iv=0$ otherwise. The finite word-object induction treats every marked whisker and every factor map. Thus $J$ meets the downward corner in exactly the ordinary first-strand ideal.

The algebraic right-append kernel agrees explicitly. Set $K_0=Se(\beta,i)/Sa(x_1)R(\beta)e(\beta,i)$ and $K_1=Se(i,\beta)/Sa(x_2)R_1(\beta)e(i,\beta)$. PBW makes them finite right $R^a(\beta)[t]$-projectives. Right multiplication $P=a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_n$ is bilinear; its counterpart $Q=g_n\cdots g_1$ uses the source intertwiners and satisfies $QP=\sum_\nu a_i(t)\prod_{\nu_a\ne i}Q_{i\nu_a}(t,x_a)e(\nu)$, with a unit leading scalar. Hence P is injective. The full-transfer PBW coset gives $\operatorname{im}P=\ker(K_0\to R^a(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i))$; shorter cosets lie in the prefix ideal. This is also valid ungraded for arbitrary monic $a_j$. It identifies the formal quotient's word corners with the actual cyclotomic corners in dependency order. All quotient objects are summands of finite sums of negative words: move formal H through the last downward letter by mixed commutation or the sign-correct EF retract and induct on word length, starting from $H_iv=0$. Thus the idempotent-completed formal quotient is the category of actual word projectives. Right appending is the actual induction, and its first adjoint is actual basic restriction by tensor-Hom uniqueness; the rho/dot formulas fix the second maps coherently under this same identification.

Finally evaluate each formal unit/counit on the regular algebra, which is the finite sum of word idempotent projectives. Naturality with its homogeneous right multiplications (and shifts) makes each evaluated map a homogeneous bimodule map. Their two triangle identities on the regular objects are equalities of those bimodule maps. Tensoring them with any graded module therefore gives units/counits with the same triangles on all graded modules, not only word projectives. The crossing-mate equality similarly is an equality of bimodule maps and extends by tensoring. Forget the internal degrees after arbitrary inhomogeneous monic coefficient specialization; all monic, dual-basis, residue, companion, cap-off and kernel identities remain algebraic identities. No graded highest-weight action is inferred for that deformation. At every stage the finite-dimensional/root-string supplier and projectivity/commutator suppliers are algebraic prerequisites; a symmetric/Frobenius or Grothendieck/crystal theorem is never used.

items.title: Normalized cyclotomic functors give an integrable quantum action
items.statement: For the standard graded quotient over arbitrary $k$ and graded admissible $Q$, let $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$. On projective $K_0$ take $F_i=F_i^{\rm basic}$ and $E_i=q_i^{1-h}E_i^{\rm basic}$ on input $\beta+i$ to output $\beta$. On module $G_0$ take the KK action $E_i=E_i^{\rm basic}$ and $F_i=q_i^{1-h}F_i^{\rm basic}$ on input $\beta$; also the canonical action with the SAME shifts as projectives. The torus acts on root component $\beta$ by $K_a=q^{\langle a,\Lambda-\beta\rangle}$. Each action satisfies all mixed relations, and $E_i,F_i$ are locally nilpotent. After scalar extension to $\mathbb Q(q)$ these are integrable type-one $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules. This does not assert a decomposition into finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ submodules and does not cover ungraded monic deformations.
items.strategy:
Projectivity supplies exact functors and preservation of finite projectives, so the displayed shifts give $A$-linear operators. In the basic commutator at target $\beta$, multiply $EF$ by $q_i^{1-h}$; the $q_i^{-2}FE$ term becomes precisely the normalized $FE$ at its changed target, and identity terms become $\sum_{k=0}^{h-1}q_i^{1-h+2k}=[h]_i$. The negative case gives the signed counterpart. In the KK representation action the same factors are instead carried by $F$; in the canonical representation action they are carried by $E$, so the same computation holds. Unequal-color basic crossing shift $q^{-b_{ij}}$ cancels the change of the normalizing $h_i$ under removing/adding $j$.
Restriction lowers height. The dot/root-string lemma gives $R^\Lambda(\beta+ni)=0$ for large $n$, so induction is locally nilpotent componentwise. Every Grothendieck element has finite root support and the displayed torus labels are correct. The general mixed/local-nilpotence lemma proves BOTH full symmetrizable Serre families by finite rank-one Hom adjoint modules, giving the unique rational quantum action without an A2 or rank-two local-finiteness assumption. All these steps precede vacuum generation and the integral highest-module identification, so no cyclic dependency is used.

items.statement:
On the generic graded KLR algebra define $\rho(e(\nu))=e(\operatorname{rev}\nu)$,
$\rho(x_a)=x_{n+1-a}$, $\rho(\tau_a)=-\tau_{n-a}$. This is a degree-preserving
ALGEBRA AUTOMORPHISM with $\rho^2=1$, commuting with the generator-fixing
anti-involution $\psi$. It maps $e(\nu)Re(\eta)$ to
$e(\operatorname{rev}\nu)Re(\operatorname{rev}\eta)$. Twisting LEFT modules by
$a\cdot m=\rho(a)m$ is an equivalence and commutes with finite vector duality
and projective Hom duality. Its separated-block formula is
$\rho^*\operatorname{Ind}(M,N)\cong\operatorname{Ind}(\rho^*N,\rho^*M)$,
without a shift. Under $\gamma:U_A^-\to K_0(R)$ it induces the quantum
multiplication-reversing star, fixing every $F_i$ and $q$. The first
cyclotomic generator maps to $a_{\nu_1}(x_n)e(\operatorname{rev}\nu)$, with the
SAME original first color. Thus it identifies the first- and last-strand
quotients; preservation of the first ideal itself is not asserted in general.

items.statement: For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any degree-zero field and admissible graded real symmetrizable KLR datum, every block $B=R^\Lambda(\beta)$ is finite-dimensional, all dots are nilpotent, and $R^\Lambda(\beta+n\alpha_i)=0$ for large $n$. Put $\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$. A nonzero block has a perfect symmetric homogeneous functional $\operatorname{tr}_\beta:B\to k$ of degree $t_\beta=-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)$; on a zero block perfectness is vacuous and the functional is zero. Thus $DB\cong B\{t_\beta\}$ as graded bimodules. For finite projective $P$, with $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,B)^\psi$, one has $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{t_\beta\}$, so vector duality preserves projectives. This does not assert $P^\#=P$ for every shifted projective, nor self-duality of every indecomposable finite module. For arbitrary monic deformation polynomials the separate conclusion is finite-dimensional and symmetric UNGRADED, with finite root strings and monic dot annihilators; nilpotence and homogeneous trace degree are not asserted. In rank one the standard trace is the top coefficient on $k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ and has degree $-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$.

items.title: Canonical elementary crystal extraction and highest-weight survivors
items.statement: For every real symmetrizable Cartan datum, the canonical negative-half crystal has strict elementary embeddings Psi_i(b)=bar b tensor b_i(-c_i(b)), where c_i(b)=epsilon_i(star b), bar b=(e_i^star)^c_i(b)b, c_i(bar b)=0, and every nonvacuum vertex has positive extraction for some i. The negative-half reversal star permutes B(infinity) without signs; this unsigned conclusion is proved from the existing signed lattice theorem and positive highest-weight tensor residues, not assumed. The survivors of pi_lambda are exactly c_i(b)<=lambda_i for all i; with weight lambda+wt(b), inherited raising and surviving lowering, and epsilon/phi, they are B(lambda). Any two lowering-generated, everywhere-lowerable negative crystals with strict nonpositive elementary extractions and positive extraction at every nonvacuum vertex are uniquely isomorphic by their lowering words; the proof uses finite color cycles and terminates after a height bound. Consequently for any field and any general homogeneous nondegenerate Q of the first two lemmas, the shift-orbit simple-module crystal is canonically B(infinity), its first-strand cyclotomic simple graph is B(lambda), and the graph labeled by indecomposable projective COVERS P(S) is the same graph under the unscaled cover–simple pairing. Projective crystal operators here mean operators transported on cover labels; no arbitrary #-dual-of-simple identification, generic global-basis theorem, or independent linear Kashiwara action on the projective class basis is asserted.
items.strategy:
## Right strings and the adapted survivor criterion, initially with signs

Define the right string operators by star conjugating the left normalized Kashiwara operators. Because star is an isometry of the actual crystal lattice and signed crystal set, every positive crystal residue b lies in exactly one right-string position c_i(b)>=0. On a lattice lift u one has

    u=sum_(n>=0) u_n F_i^(n),   u_n in ker(star e_i' star),

with every u_n in the crystal lattice, and modulo q only the component n=c_i(b) is nonzero. Its top coefficient has residue ±bar b for some positive crystal residue bar b with c_i(bar b)=0. For the negative half the lattice-component argument is proved directly by the same finite tail calculation as the module string lemma: if u=sum_n F_i^(n)v_n, set T_n=e-tilde_i^n u; then v_n=T_n-f-tilde_i T_(n+1) lies in the lattice. Induction on the largest position, using the residue partial inverse, shows that a basis residue has exactly one nonzero component and that its top residue is positive. Root height makes the tails finite. This proves the half version without applying an integrable-module-only Statement to U^-. Conjugating this argument through the signed lattice theorem gives the asserted signed right version, without assuming unsigned star. The integer c_i(b) is epsilon_i of the absolute value of star b.

The field right ideal U^- F_i^t is the direct sum of right-string positions n>=t. Its adapted global subset is therefore precisely the positive indices b with c_i(b)>=t: conjugate the already proved left-string adapted global subset through star, whose possible signs do not affect which A-basis vectors span the ideal. The based quotient's field kernel is the sum of these right ideals at t=lambda_i+1. Since all are adapted to ONE global basis, their sum is the span of the union of their basis subsets. Therefore

    pi_lambda(b)!=0 iff c_i(b)<=lambda_i for every i.    (A)

This proves the highest-weight survivor criterion already with signed star. It neither assumes unsigned star nor infers an adapted intersection from an arbitrary linear sum. The surviving residues are bijective with B(lambda) by the existing based quotient/grand loop. Raising cannot turn a survivor into a killed nonzero residue: if e_i b were killed, the ALL-residue lowering identity pi_lambda(f_i(e_i b))=f_i pi_lambda(e_i b)=0 and the negative-half partial inverse f_i e_i b=b would force b killed, a contradiction. Thus every nonzero raising iterate of a survivor survives. Combining this with the surviving-residue raising identity proves equality of the entire raising lengths, epsilon_i(pi_lambda b)=epsilon_i(b), including the zero endpoint. This supplies the precise statistic identification used later in the finite-model construction without circularly using elementary embeddings. Raising on survivors and surviving lowering are exactly these existing projection compatibilities. The shifted statistics are epsilon_i(b) and epsilon_i(b)+<h_i,lambda+wt(b)> because B(lambda) is the actual highest-weight module crystal; raising preservation gives epsilon equality, and its rank-one formula gives phi.

## Canonical elementary embedding by finite highest-weight tensor models

Fix color i and a finite set of lowering words of height at most H. Work in the regularized finite support. Choose lambda_i=0 and lambda_j large for j!=i, large enough that no right ideal for those j meets any relevant root component of height at most H+1. Choose N>H+1. The total label lambda+N Lambda_i is then large at every relevant color, so its projection identifies the canonical B(infinity) vertices and all edges under consideration with the corresponding finite-degree vertices of B(lambda+N Lambda_i). Apply the strict highest-weight tensor embedding into B(lambda) tensor B(N Lambda_i).

Throughout these finite lowering paths the second factor is a pure i-string f_i^m u_(N Lambda_i). Indeed initially it is highest. For j!=i its epsilon_j is0 at every pure i-string position: E_j commutes with F_i and kills the highest vector, so all such vectors are E_j-highest. The first factor's phi_j is positive and larger than any second epsilon_j in the bounded degree, because lambda_j is chosen large. Thus both lowering and raising of any j!=i act on the first factor. Color i preserves the pure i-string form. Its string endpoint N is not reached in this height bound.

Lift the first residue b_1 uniquely to its surviving positive residue b' in B(infinity). Replace the second pure i-position m by b_i(-m) in the elementary crystal. The finite tensor rules become exactly those on B(infinity) tensor B_i: for i, lambda_i=0 means the first phi_i is epsilon_i(b')+<h_i,wt(b')>, and the second epsilon_i is m. For j!=i the elementary statistics are -infinity, so its tensor rule selects the first factor, just as the large-lambda finite model does. The finite tensor epsilon formula reduces to epsilon_j(b') for j!=i because lambda_j is large; for i it reduces to max(epsilon_i(b'),m-<h_i,wt(b')>). Root weights add to wt(b')-m alpha_i. Thus the replacement preserves the generic weight, epsilon and formal phi statistics as well as every considered operator.

This construction is independent of lambda,N WITHOUT assuming a stabilization theorem. Define its candidate value on a lowering word w by computing w(u_infinity tensor b_i(0)) using the actual generic tensor rules. The preceding finite-model argument shows that this computation agrees with the replacement of the finite tensor image for every bounded path. If two words w,w' give the same b in B(infinity), choose one common finite bound and one common pair lambda,N. Their images in B(lambda+N Lambda_i) coincide, hence their strict tensor images coincide, and the unique surviving lifts of their first factors coincide. Therefore the candidate generic tensor values coincide. Conversely if the candidate values coincide, choose the same finite model for the two words; its first-factor projections and second positions coincide, and injectivity of Phi followed by the large-label projection identification gives w u_infinity=w' u_infinity. This proves a well-defined injective Psi_i, independent of all choices.

For lowering use the same finite model on a word and that word with one appended operator. For raising use a model containing the vertex, its raising neighbor if nonzero, and the next boundary; strictness of finite Phi and the already checked branch/statistic formulas give Psi_i(e_j b)=e_j Psi_i(b), including zero. Hence

    Psi_i:B(infinity)->B(infinity) tensor B_i

is strict, sends the vacuum to u_infinity tensor b_i(0), and every elementary coordinate is nonpositive. This is an actual finite-word construction, rather than a citation to Kashiwara Theorem8.2.

## Identifying the elementary coordinate with the right-string index

The remaining coordinate identification can be checked on the coproduct rather than assumed from unsigned star. For a homogeneous P of root beta, the coefficient of one i in the second tensor factor of Delta(P), after extracting its toral K_i, is e_i''(P). On homogeneous root beta this derivative is

    e_i''(P)=q_i^(<h_i,beta>-2) (star e_i' star)(P).

Check this first on a generator. Both sides then satisfy the same twisted deletion rule, with prefix versus suffix twists interchanged; the displayed homogeneous scalar converts one rule into the other. Hence their kernels agree. Coassociativity or repeated deletion shows that every higher pure-second-i coefficient is a nonzero field scalar multiple of the corresponding repeated derivative; it therefore vanishes on P in the right-string kernel. Thus projecting Delta(P) onto the terms with pure i root degree in the second factor leaves exactly P tensor1.

Apply this to the right expansion u=sum_n u_n F_i^(n) above, acting on v_lambda tensor v_(N Lambda_i) with lambda_i=0. Every mixed-color second-factor term has a different second root degree and is removed by the pure-i projection. For u_n in the right kernel only u_n tensor1 survives that projection. In Delta F_i^(n), every term whose first divided power F_i^(a) has a>0 kills v_lambda before u_n acts. The remaining term is K_i^n tensor F_i^(n), and K_i^n v_lambda=v_lambda because lambda_i=0. Therefore the exact pure-second-i projection is

    sum_n pi_lambda(u_n) tensor F_i^(n)v_(N Lambda_i).   (B)

No uncontrolled q shift occurs in this formula with the actual native coproduct. The derivative equality above is only used to identify the kernel; scalar rescalings do not change it.

The coefficient u_c, c=c_i(b), has signed positive crystal residue ±bar b with right index0. Its projection at lambda_i=0 survives by (A); all other coordinates survive because lambda_j is large. Thus its projected residue is nonzero. Every n!=c coefficient has zero crystal residue. Formula (B) consequently has exactly one nonzero pure-i tensor residue, at position c. On the other hand Phi(pi_(lambda+N Lambda_i)b) is a positive pure-i tensor residue by the finite model. It follows that its elementary coordinate m is exactly c_i(b), and that the top right-string coefficient u_c has POSITIVE residue bar b, not negative. Thus

    Psi_i(b)=bar b tensor b_i(-c_i(b)),
    c_i(bar b)=0,  b=(f_i^right)^(c_i(b)) bar b.          (C)

In particular every nonvacuum b has positive extraction at some i: star b is a signed nonvacuum crystal residue, and the canonical lowering-generated crystal has a nonzero raising direction on its absolute value.

## Unsigned star follows rather than being assumed

Induct on root height. The vacuum is fixed by star. For a positive-height b choose i with c_i(b)>0. Formula (C) gives b=(f_i^right)^c bar b with bar b a POSITIVE residue of strictly smaller height. Apply star:

    star b=f_i^c(star bar b).

By induction star bar b is positive, and canonical lowering preserves positive crystal residues. Therefore star b is positive. Since star is an involution, it permutes B(infinity) bijectively without signs. This proves unsigned star for every real symmetrizable datum from the actual signed theorem plus tensor positivity. Then c_i(b)=epsilon_i(star b) is the usual epsilon_i^star, and (C) is the exact canonical elementary extraction formula. The proof does not invoke a symmetric-type geometric basis.

## Identification of the generic and cyclotomic module crystals

the preceding local one-step and jump/embedding lemmas construct the generic module strict elementary embeddings, with extraction coordinate epsilon_i^L and positive extraction on every nonvacuum module. Both its graph and the canonical graph just constructed are generated by lowering words from their vacua and have every lowering operator nonzero. The finite-extraction comparison lemma proved next identifies the two graphs uniquely by lowering words. Strictness also forces their elementary extraction coordinates to agree: the comparison tensor identity holds on the vacuum and on every lowering word, so

    epsilon_i^L(M)=epsilon_i^star(b_M).

The local one-step lemma's first-dot criterion identifies the cyclotomic module vertices with epsilon_i^star(b_M)<=lambda_i. Equation (A) identifies exactly that subset with the surviving canonical vertices, hence with B(lambda). Existing projection compatibility proves the raising and surviving-lowering correspondence, while The local jump lemma's actual normal-length formula gives the canonical epsilon/phi data. This proves the full all-field/general homogeneous-Q simple crystal theorem, using exactly the stated local quantum and algebra suppliers. Projective vertices are labeled by the indecomposable projective COVER P(M) of each simple M. The cover–simple Hom pairing transports this graph: E/F crystal labels on covers mean P(e-tilde M), P(f-tilde M), with zero when the simple label is zero. This does not identify P(M) with an arbitrary # dual of M. Independently defined projective Kashiwara operators still require their exact leading-term convention.

## Finite-extraction comparison proof

There is a smaller recognition contract for this application, whose proof is elementary. Suppose C and D are crystals, each generated from its unique weight-zero vertex by lowering words, every f_i is everywhere nonzero, and each has strict elementary embeddings Psi_i with nonpositive elementary coordinates and a positive coordinate for some i on every nonvacuum vertex. Assume the weight support of a vertex is finite and extraction subtracts a nonnegative multiple of alpha_i from its root weight. Then there is a unique crystal isomorphism C=D carrying the two vacua to each other.

Proof. Fix a finite color set containing the support of a lowering word. Cycle through these colors, applying Psi_i to the current first factor, and leave every elementary tensor factor already extracted in place. Tensoring a strict embedding with identity maps is strict: for each color the tensor max formulas preserve epsilon/phi and weight, hence preserve the branch inequality including equality. Therefore every finite composite is strict and injective. Each extraction lowers the nonnegative height of the first factor by its elementary coordinate c. If an entire cycle makes no extraction from a nonvacuum factor, that factor is unchanged throughout the cycle, yet its support has a color with positive extraction, contradiction. Thus after at most the starting height many cycles (and one harmless final cycle) the first factor is the vacuum. Extraction of absent colors is zero: a nonzero alpha_i extraction would give a residual root weight with negative alpha_i coefficient, forbidden. Consequently this finite procedure works in both crystals using the same finite color cycle.

For a word w of length h, use h+1 cycles. Every prefix has height at most h, so both images of every prefix have vacuum first factor. Strictness computes the image of w by applying that same lowering word to the same tensor of a vacuum and elementary zero vertices. While the underlying vacua belong to different crystals, their weights and epsilon/phi are identical and their raising operators vanish; at each intermediate prefix the first factor is still the vacuum, so a nonzero lowering operation cannot take place in that first factor. All operations occur in the identical elementary factors, and the resulting elementary coordinates are identical. If two words w,w' produce the same vertex in C, use a common finite color set and enough cycles for both lengths; their identical C images give identical coordinate tensors, hence identical D images and, by injectivity, identical D vertices. Interchanging C and D gives the converse. Mapping a lowering word in C to that word in D is therefore a well-defined bijection. It preserves lowering by construction, raising by partial inverses, weights by word content, and epsilon/phi because the common strict finite tensor embeddings preserve these statistics. Uniqueness follows from lowering generation. This proves the lemma.

items.title: Cyclotomic projective covers and dualities descend through the quotient
items.statement:
Let $A=R(\beta)$ and $B=A/J$ be the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient.
For an indecomposable finite graded projective generic cover $P(S)$,
$B\otimes_AP(S)$ is its same-head indecomposable $B$-cover if $JS=0$, and is
zero otherwise. Every graded simple/indecomposable projective $B$-orbit arises
this way, and distinct surviving heads do not merge. Finite projective Hom
duality commutes with this base change, and finite vector duality commutes with
inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual
simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels
$h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and
$T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_BS)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is
bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Extension induces a surjection on
projective $K_0$. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal premise
is used.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** apply the quotient adjunction to projective covers, control indecomposability through the local degree-zero endomorphism rings, then compare the two dualities and the two pairing forms.

1.1 Base change of projectives and covers. A finite graded projective $P$ is a retract of a finite sum of shifted copies of $A$, so $B\otimes_AP$ is a retract of a finite sum of shifted copies of $B$: it is finite graded projective. The quotient adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,B\otimes_AP')=\operatorname{Hom}_B(B\otimes_AP,B\otimes_AP')$, and every degree-zero endomorphism of $B\otimes_AP$ lifts through the canonical map $P\to B\otimes_AP$; endomorphisms preserve $JP$, so the induced map $\operatorname{End}^0_A(P)\to\operatorname{End}^0_B(B\otimes_AP)$ is a surjective ring homomorphism. If $P$ is indecomposable, its finite-dimensional local degree-zero endomorphism ring has no nontrivial idempotent, so a nonzero quotient has none either: $B\otimes_AP$ is zero or indecomposable. If $JS=0$, the old cover map factors through $P/JP$ and remains essential (a submodule of $B\otimes_AP$ mapping onto $S$ pulls back to a submodule of $P$ mapping onto $S$; essentiality of the old cover makes it all of $P$), so $B\otimes_AP$ is the projective cover of $S$ with the same head. If $JS\ne0$ and $B\otimes_AP\ne0$, finite dimension [F3] supplies a simple quotient, which must be the unique head $S$; as a $B$-module that quotient is annihilated by $J$, forcing $JS=0$ and contradicting the assumption, so $B\otimes_AP=0$. [F1, F3]

2.1 Every $B$-orbit arises and heads do not merge. Every simple $B$-module is a simple $A$-module by inflation, and its descended cover $B\otimes_AP(S)$ is a nonzero cover, so every $B$-simple/projective orbit arises this way. Distinct surviving heads remain distinct after quotienting because an isomorphism of the descended covers induces an isomorphism of their simple heads as $B$-modules, hence also as $A$-modules after inflation; hence the surviving projective-cover shift orbits cannot merge, and extension of scalars is surjective on projective $K_0$. [step 1.1, F1]

3.1 Dualities. For finite $P$, evaluation on shifted free modules and restriction to retracts identifies $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B\otimes_AP,B)=\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,A)\otimes_AB$, and applying the generator-fixing anti-involution $\psi$ gives $(B\otimes_AP)^\#=B\otimes_AP^\#$. Inflation does not change the finite vector duality $D_\psi$ of a simple, since the underlying vector space and the $\psi$-action are unchanged. The choice-free normalization clauses of [F2] therefore carry the unique $\#$-self-dual generic covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual simples to unique normalized $B$-covers and simples. [step 2.1, F2]

4.1 The two pairings. For normalized labels, $h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)=q^a$ in a single shift $a$ because $\operatorname{End}(S)=k$ absolutely, while distinct heads give zero; assigning the simple's shift makes $h=\delta_{P,S}$. Similarly $T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_BS)=\delta_{P,S}$ by finite-projective evaluation and $D(P^\psi\otimes S)=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,D_\psi S)$ for evaluation of a tensor functional; $T$ is bilinear in the two arguments and $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ is first-bar sesquilinear. Extension of scalars induces the surjection on projective $K_0$ by step 2.1. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal statement is used. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F2] ∎

items.title: Cyclotomic diagram duality and graded module duals
items.statement: For the standard graded quotient $B=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $\psi$ is the descended anti-involution fixing $e(\nu),x_a,\tau_a$. For a finite module $M$ define $D_\psi M=\operatorname{HOM}_k(M,k)^\psi$, with $(af)(m)=f(\psi(a)m)$. For a finite graded PROJECTIVE $P$ define instead $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,B)^\psi$. Both reverse internal shifts and are involutive on their respective domains. They are DIFFERENT dualities; Hom duality is not applied to a nonprojective simple to produce its cover. By [[lem-cyclotomic-projective-covers-and-dualities-descend-through-the-quotient]], each simple orbit has a unique $D_\psi$-self-dual representative $S$, and its unique normalized cover $P$ with $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)=k$ is $\#$-self-dual. These are the normalizations in the based statements. No self-dual shift is asserted for every indecomposable finite module. The symmetric theorem additionally gives $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)\}$; it does not change the canonical projective normalization.
items.strategy: The cyclotomic ideal is $\psi$-stable because its individual first-strand polynomial generators are fixed. Finite vector-space evaluation proves the double $D_\psi$ identity. Evaluation on shifted free modules, then finite retracts, proves the double projective Hom-dual identity. Quotient Hom basechange carries generic normalized projective covers to their nonzero normalized cyclotomic covers, and inflation carries the normalized vector-dual simples unchanged. The quotient-cover lemma proves the normalizations and the unscaled pairing without a Frobenius premise. The trace theorem relates the two dualities only afterward. In rank one $B=k[x]/x^\lambda$, $B^\#=B$ but $D_\psi B=B\{-2d_i(\lambda-1)\}$, illustrating the distinction.

items.title: The vacuum projective is a highest-weight generator
items.statement:
For the standard graded quotient, $1_\Lambda=[k]\in K_0(R^\Lambda(0))$ is a
nonzero highest-weight vector of weight $\Lambda$ for the normalized action.
Every finite projective is a finite retract of a sum of shifted word
projectives $P_\nu=R^\Lambda(\beta)e(\nu)$, and
$[P_\nu]=F_{\nu_n}\cdots F_{\nu_1}1_\Lambda$ for right append. The stronger
integral generation statement is by DIVIDED words: the classes
$F_{i_r}^{(a_r)}\cdots F_{i_1}^{(a_1)}1_\Lambda$ span $K_0(R^\Lambda)$ over
$A$. Thus $U_A^-1_\Lambda=K_0(R^\Lambda)$. The retract statement alone is not
claimed to make ordinary word classes an $A$-spanning set.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** check the vacuum's highest-weight property directly, realise every finite projective as a retract of word projectives, and transfer divided generation from the generic negative half through the quotient.

1.1 The vacuum is a nonzero highest-weight vector. The rank-zero block is $R^\Lambda(0)=k$, so $1_\Lambda=[k]$ is nonzero; restriction from root zero has zero target, so $E_i1_\Lambda=0$ for every $i$; and the torus acts on the root-zero component by $q^{\langle a,\Lambda\rangle}$, so its weight is $\Lambda$. [F1]

2.1 Word projectives and retracts. The finitely many word idempotents of a root block sum to its unit, so the regular module is the sum of the corresponding word projectives and every finite projective is a retract of a finite sum of shifted copies. The append bimodule sends the word $\nu$ to $\nu i$, and since operators in a composite act from right to left, $[P_\nu]=F_{\nu_n}\cdots F_{\nu_1}1_\Lambda$. This is a statement about retracts of ordinary word projectives; it does not by itself make ordinary word classes an $A$-spanning set. [step 1.1, F2]

3.1 Divided generation. The quotient-cover lemma [F3] makes extension of scalars surjective on split $K_0$, so it suffices to generate the generic $K_0$ by extensions of divided words. The generic negative-half categorification identifies generic $K_0$ with $U_A^-$ and its divided-power projectives with the divided generators; their extensions are the cyclotomic divided functors applied to the vacuum, so the classes $F_{i_r}^{(a_r)}\cdots F_{i_1}^{(a_1)}1_\Lambda$ span $K_0(R^\Lambda)$ over $A$. This does not divide by a quantum factorial: $F_i^a=[a]_{q_i}!F_i^{(a)}$ has a generally nonunit coefficient, which is exactly why the stronger generation statement must use divided words. Combining this generation with the independent normalized-action result of [[lem-cyclotomic-normalized-functors-give-an-integrable-quantum-action]] gives $U_A^-1_\Lambda=K_0(R^\Lambda)$ without a circular appeal to the integral highest-weight theorem. [step 2.1, F3] ∎

items.title: Cyclotomic KLR functors define an integrable quantum action on $K_0$ and $G_0$
items.statement:
For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any field and any real symmetrizable Cartan datum with admissible graded KLR parameters, put $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $h_i(\beta)=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$, and $q_i=q^{d_i}$. On projective $K_0$ use $F_i=F_i^{\rm basic}$ and $E_i|_\beta=q_i^{-1-h_i(\beta)}E_i^{\rm basic}$; on module $G_0$ use either the SAME canonical normalization, or the Kang--Kashiwara normalization $E_i^{\rm KK}=E_i^{\rm basic}$, $F_i^{\rm KK}|_\beta=q_i^{1-h_i(\beta)}F_i^{\rm basic}$. In all cases $K_i|_\beta=q_i^{h_i(\beta)}$. These operators satisfy the full quantum mixed and Serre relations and are locally nilpotent; their scalar extensions to $\mathbb Q(q)$ are integrable weight modules. No decomposition into finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ submodules is asserted in affine or indefinite type.
The tensor pairing $T_\beta(P,M)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}M)$ is $A$-BILINEAR and weightwise perfect in normalized projective-cover/simple bases. The Hom pairing $h(P,M)=\mathrm{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$ instead satisfies $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ and is first-bar-sesquilinear. For $T$, projective $E_i$ is adjoint to module $F_i^{\rm KK}$ and projective $F_i$ to module $E_i^{\rm KK}$. The two module actions are conjugate by the weight rescaling $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$, where $\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$.
items.strategy:
1. The normalized-action supplier combines the actual same-color categorical decomposition and unequal-color mixed crossings with finite root strings. For $E_i$ applied to input root $\beta+\alpha_i$ its exponent is $-1-h_i(\beta+\alpha_i)=1-h_i(\beta)$, exactly the target-weight normalization. Its general rank-one Hom-envelope proof gives every symmetrizable Serre relation without a rank-two finite-orbit assumption.
2. Tensor products of finite modules are finite, hence $T$ has Laurent-polynomial values. The quotient-cover lemma gives absolutely simple normalized heads and $T(P(S),S')=\delta_{S,S'}$, proving weightwise perfectness. Shifting either tensor factor multiplies by the same $q$-power; this is bilinearity, whereas finite-projective evaluation identifies $\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$ with $(P^\#)^\psi\otimes M$, giving the different Hom convention.
3. For the corner $A_\beta\to eB_{\beta+i}e$, associativity gives $T_B(FP,M)=T_A(P,EM)$ for the BASIC functors. The generator-fixing anti-involution flips balanced tensors, so $T_B(P,FM)=T_A(EP,M)$ as well: the corner factors become $eB$ and $Be$ in opposite order and multiplication gives the evaluation isomorphism. Multiplying the second identity by $q_i^{1-h_i(\beta)}$ gives the first normalized adjoint statement; the first identity gives the other. This uses neither the Frobenius theorem nor the highest-weight $K_0$ theorem.
4. Adding $i$ changes defect by $d_i(h_i(\beta)-1)$. Consequently multiplication by $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$ conjugates the canonical module action to the KK action in both directions. The weight action is unchanged. All assertions here are about the standard homogeneous quotient, not arbitrary monic deformations.

items.title: The cyclotomic projective $K_0$ is the integral highest-weight module
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. For the standard homogeneous graded quotient over any field, with arbitrary real symmetrizable Cartan datum and admissible graded KLR parameters, there is a unique $U_A$-module isomorphism $\phi:K_0(\mathrm{Proj}\,R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ sending $1_\Lambda$ to $v_\Lambda$ and intertwining all normalized $E_i,F_i,K_i$ and divided powers. In particular $K_0$ is free over $A$. On the NEGATIVE half the vacuum map has exact kernel
$$\ker(U_A^-\to K_0(R^\Lambda))=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda_i}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}.$$
This is the integral negative-half presentation; neither a full-$U_A$ quotient by only $F_i^{(\lambda_i+1)}$ nor invertibility of divided-power factorials is asserted.
For projectives, the tensor form $T(P,Q)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes Q)$ transports to the highest-weight contravariant form normalized by $(v_\Lambda,v_\Lambda)=1$ and $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$, $\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}$, $\sigma(K_i)=K_i$. It is not the generic negative-half Lusztig form with a newly alleged radical.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** factor the divided vacuum map through the exact integral highest-weight presentation, prove it is an isomorphism by rational simplicity and the torsion-free source lattice, and identify the tensor form by its actual corner adjunction and normalization.

**Given:** The data of F1–F4, with AC inherited through the declared generic and quantum highest-weight suppliers.

1.1 By F1 the map $U_A^-\to K_0(R^\Lambda)$, $u\mapsto u1_\Lambda$, is surjective. For every $s>\lambda_i$, the staircase idempotent in F3 is divisible on the left by $x_1^{\lambda_i}$, since $s-1\ge\lambda_i$, and therefore is zero in the standard quotient. The generator-fixing anti-involution preserves its cyclotomic ideal, so the dual projector defining the divided-power projective is zero as well. Hence $F_i^{(s)}1_\Lambda=0$ without dividing by a quantum factorial. All translates $U_A^-F_i^{(s)}$ therefore lie in its kernel. The exact integral projection presentation in F3 gives a well-defined surjective $A$-linear map $f:V_A(\Lambda)\to K_0(R^\Lambda)$ sending $v_\Lambda$ to $1_\Lambda$ and every divided word to the corresponding divided-functor class. [F1, F3, construct, algebra]

1.2 The anti-involution identifies $P^\psi\otimes Q$ with $Q^\psi\otimes P$ by interchanging the factors, so the projective tensor form $T$ is symmetric and $A$-bilinear. Different root blocks pair by zero. The basic corner identities of F2 give $T(F_iP,Q)=T(P,E_i^{\rm basic}Q)$ and $T(E_i^{\rm basic}P,Q)=T(P,F_iQ)$. At input $\beta+\alpha_i$ and output $\beta$, put $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$. Projective $E_i=q_i^{1-h}E_i^{\rm basic}$ and $q_i^{-1}K_iE_i=q_i^{h-1}E_i=E_i^{\rm basic}$ on this target. Thus the first identity is $T(F_iP,Q)=T(P,\sigma(F_i)Q)$. [F2, F4, algebra]


1.3 The integral positive operators are defined as well. On $n$-fold basic restriction the last $n$ equal-color dots and crossings give a nil-Hecke action commuting with the target algebra. Its graded matrix-column decomposition in F3 expresses this restriction as $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of an idempotent summand, with the symmetric centering of the polynomial column. Restriction preserves finite projectives by F2, so this summand is finite projective. Multiplying it by the integral grading shift from the $n$ successive $E_i$ normalizations realizes the rational operator $E_i^n/[n]_i!$ on $K_0$; thus it preserves $K_0$ without inverting the factorial in $A$. Negative divided powers are realized by the analogous induction idempotents of F3. A toral binomial acts on an integral weight by $\prod_{s=1}^t[m+c-s+1]_i/[s]_i$. For $m+c\ge0$ this is the integral Gaussian binomial (or zero), and for $m+c<0$ it is $(-1)^t\binom{-(m+c)+t-1}{t}_i$, again integral by [[lem-quantum-pascal-recurrence-and-gaussian-integrality]]. Hence the full $U_A$ acts on $K_0$; its relations follow from the rational action because the cover basis in F4 makes $K_0$ torsion-free. [F2, F3, F4, F5, algebra]


2.1 The quotient-cover bases in F4 make $K_0$ free over $A$; in particular its nonzero vacuum stays nonzero after tensoring with $\mathbb Q(q)$. By F2 the rationalized target is an integrable cyclic highest-weight module of weight $\Lambda$. The universality and ordinary simplicity in F3 identify it with $V(\Lambda)$ by the unique map preserving the highest vector. This map is the rationalization of $f$, since both agree on every divided word. Thus $f$ becomes an isomorphism after localization. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 An element $z\in\ker f$ maps to zero on localization, so some nonzero $a\in A$ kills $z$. The source $V_A(\Lambda)$ is an actual submodule of the vector space $V(\Lambda)$ over the fraction field, by F3, and is consequently torsion-free. Hence $z=0$, proving $f$ injective. Its inverse $\phi$ is the required integral isomorphism; the original vacuum map has exactly the integral projection kernel in the Statement. The rational isomorphism intertwines all normalized positive, negative and toral operators. Each difference of their integral operator maps has zero localization, and the target $K_0$ is torsion-free by F4, so the equality holds integrally, including the actual divided powers. Uniqueness follows from divided-word generation. [F1, F3, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 For the second identity, take $P$ at root $\beta+\alpha_i$ and $Q$ at root $\beta$. Its normalization yields $T(E_iP,Q)=q_i^{1-h}T(P,F_iQ)$. On $Q$, $q_iF_iK_i^{-1}=q_i^{1-h}F_i$, so this is $T(E_iP,Q)=T(P,\sigma(E_i)Q)$. The torus is scalar on each root component and preserves its label, giving toral contravariance. The vacuum tensor product is $k$, of norm one. Transported by $\phi$, these identities and symmetry give exactly the normalized highest-weight contravariant form; uniqueness in F4 identifies it. This uses the highest-weight form, rather than the generic negative-half form or a supposed new radical of that form. [F2, F4, step 3.1, step 1.2, algebra]

5.1 Steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1 prove the unique integral highest-weight isomorphism and its exact divided right-power kernel in the full stated general-field/general-Cartan scope. Steps 1.2 and 4.1 prove the tensor-form assertion. Projective-cover shift orbits give the independent free $A$-basis, without treating all divided words as a basis or making a quantum factorial invertible. AC is inherited only through the declared generic categorification and quantum highest-weight suppliers; the localization, torsion-free kernel and finite corner computations introduce no further choice. [step 3.1, step 4.1, F4] ∎

items.title: The cyclotomic module $G_0$ is the restricted dual integral highest-weight module
items.statement:
For the same standard homogeneous general-field/general-Cartan parameters as the integral projective theorem, the tensor pairing $T(P,M)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes M)$ is weightwise perfect and $A$-bilinear, with normalized cover/simple dual bases. Its associated map
$$\Psi_{\rm can}:G_0(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow V_A(\Lambda)^\vee=\bigoplus_\beta\operatorname{Hom}_A(V_A(\Lambda)_{\Lambda-\beta},A),\qquad \Psi_{\rm can}(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$$
is an isomorphism to the RESTRICTED weight dual, identified inside $V(\Lambda)$ using the highest-weight contravariant form. It intertwines the CANONICAL module action having the same normalization as projective $K_0$, and sends normalized simple classes to the form-dual projective basis. The KK module action is also sound, but its intertwiner is $\Psi_{\rm KK}|_\beta=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}\Psi_{\rm can}|_\beta$. Thus an unrescaled KK identification is not asserted to send simples to the upper global basis. The Hom pairing is instead first-bar-sesquilinear, $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$; this does not alter the bilinear tensor-dual identification.
items.strategy:
1. Finite blocks have finitely many absolutely simple graded shift orbits and normalized projective covers, by the quotient-cover lemma. Exactness of projective tensor pairing and the unscaled diagonal values give perfectness over $A$ on each weight. Consequently $G_0$ is free with these simple classes, and the functional map is an isomorphism to the weightwise dual of $K_0$. Take the DIRECT SUM over weights, not the full unrestricted product dual.
2. Transport $K_0$ by $\phi$. Its tensor form is the actual highest-weight contravariant form with $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$. From tensor adjunction, $T(P,F_i^{\rm basic}M)=T(E_i^{\rm basic}P,M)=T(\sigma(F_i)P,M)$; the analogous normalized $E_i$ identity is $T(P,E_i^{\rm can}M)=T(\sigma(E_i)P,M)$. These are precisely the restricted contravariant-dual action. Thus $\Psi_{\rm can}$ intertwines, without identifying an ordinary transpose action with the wrong quantum normalization.
3. The defect difference computed in the action theorem shows that $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}\Psi_{\rm can}$ intertwines KK $E$ and $F$. In rank one $\lambda=2$, the middle form norm is $1+q^2$, so the canonical upper vector is $Fv/(1+q^2)$ and its $E$ image is $q^{-1}v$. This matches $E^{\rm can}=q^{-1}\mathrm{Res}$, whereas KK $E=\mathrm{Res}$ sends the middle simple to the vacuum without that factor; the defect rescaling accounts for it.
4. On normalized covers $P^\#=P$, so $h$ and $T$ have the same diagonal simple values. On arbitrary shifted classes their scalar rules differ exactly as stated. This establishes the duality claim with the genuine restricted lattice and both correct module actions.

items.title: Simple and indecomposable-projective crystals agree with $B(\Lambda)$
items.statement: For the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient over any field with the general real symmetrizable datum and graded KLR parameters, let $\mathcal B_\Lambda$ be the normalized $D_\psi$-self-dual simple classes. Set $\mathrm{wt}(S)=\Lambda-\beta$, $\varepsilon_i(S)=\max\{r:(E_i^{\rm basic})^rS\ne0\}$ and $\varphi_i(S)=\varepsilon_i(S)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(S)\rangle$. For $\varepsilon_i>0$, define $\widetilde e_iS$ by the unique simple isomorphism type in the socle of one-step right restriction, with its unique self-dual normalization; define $\widetilde f_iS$ by the simple head of right induction when nonzero, otherwise zero. The one-step socle/head is one shifted copy, not a quantum-factorial multiplicity. These data form a crystal canonically isomorphic to $B(\Lambda)$, with vacuum sent to $u_\Lambda$. The normalized indecomposable projectives carry the same crystal by their normalized simple heads and covers. The projective graph here is explicitly transported from these labels, rather than obtained by applying linear Kashiwara operators to an unspecified projective basis. The highest-weight quotient has simple survivors exactly when $\varepsilon_i^{\rm LEFT}(S)\le\lambda_i$ for every $i$.
items.strategy:
1. Inflate a cyclotomic simple to the generic algebra. The one-step supplier proves the actual unique head/socle and rank-one multiplicities through the nil-Hecke matrix/corner description; its first-dot index identifies the FIRST-strand ideal criterion with $\varepsilon_i^{\rm LEFT}\le\lambda_i$. This argument uses finite-dimensional nilpotent-dot simples and works over the original field, including positive characteristic.
2. The two-color supplier proves the full general-$Q$ jump formula and strict elementary embeddings from actual shuffle filtrations, divided restriction multiplicities and explicit rank-two operators. The linear Serre relation is applied in $G_0$, not to a nonlinear simple operator. It establishes the generic crystal extraction hypotheses in every real symmetrizable type; no ADE-only or finite-rank-two-orbit argument replaces them.
3. Apply the canonical elementary-extraction/highest-weight-survivor supplier. Its positive highest-weight tensor models and unsigned star identification give the generic $B(\infty)$ labeling by RIGHT operators and identify the left-survivor subset with the canonical $B(\Lambda)$ under $\pi_\Lambda$. It proves connectedness from the vacuum, strictness and the truncation of induction at the string endpoint. If an auxiliary primitive-coroot datum is needed for sufficiently large containing weights, it has the same $A,D,Q$ and does not change the KLR algebras. Thus the displayed weight, epsilon and phi are precisely the highest-weight crystal functions.
4. The quotient-cover lemma identifies normalized covers with their simple heads bijectively, with diagonal tensor pairing. Transfer the simple arrows through this bijection. This proves the projective crystal statement and its normalized labeling without using the later lower/upper global-basis conclusions. Choice is inherited only through the declared abstract crystal/balanced-lift suppliers in the extraction step.

items.title: Cyclotomic extension of scalars respects the based quotient
items.statement:
Assume the full symmetric normalized-$d_i=1$, characteristic-zero,
loopless-quiver geometric-parameter scope of the generic global theorem, and
the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient with RIGHT append.
Let $\gamma:U_A^-\to K_0(R)$ be the approved generic categorification and
$\phi:K_0(R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ the vacuum-normalized integral
isomorphism. Then the raw extension $q_\Lambda(P)=R^\Lambda\otimes_RP$
satisfies
$$\phi[q_\Lambda(P)]=\pi_\Lambda\bigl(*(\gamma^{-1}[P])\bigr).$$
Composing extension with the generic mirror twist gives $\pi_\Lambda$ without
star. For $b\in B(\infty)$ and the generic normalized indecomposable projective
$P_b$ with $\gamma^{-1}[P_b]=G^-(b)$, raw extension is zero or a SINGLE
normalized indecomposable cyclotomic projective; its image is
$\pi_\Lambda G^-(b^*)$, which is zero or $G^-_\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda b^*)$. The
surviving cover orbits do not merge, and every normalized cyclotomic cover is
obtained. In RIGHT-simple labels $c$, the generic FIRST-recursion theorem gives
$\gamma^{-1}[P(S_c)]=G^-(c^*)$, so raw extension sends it to
$G^-_\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda c)$; these are exactly the crystal-compatible
survivor labels of the preceding theorem. The claim is for indecomposable
projectives, not every finite projective quotient.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** compare the side conventions on divided words, use the
mirror twist to convert star into the identity, and read survival and
non-merging off the cover-descent lemma.

1.1 The raw extension map on divided words. Right append sends a word $\nu_1\cdots\nu_n$ to $F_{\nu_n}\cdots F_{\nu_1}v_\Lambda$, whereas the generic multiplication convention assigns $F_{\nu_1}\cdots F_{\nu_n}$; on actual divided word classes the map is therefore $\pi_\Lambda\circ*$. Their $A$-span is all generic $K_0$ by [F1], so this determines the map integrally, giving $\phi[q_\Lambda(P)]=\pi_\Lambda(*(\gamma^{-1}[P]))$; composing with the generic mirror twist of [F2], which supplies exactly $*$ and commutes with projective Hom duality, gives $\pi_\Lambda$ without star. [F1, F2]

1.2 Positive star on the global basis. The generic mirror equivalence of [F2] preserves indecomposability and commutes with projective Hom duality, hence permutes the normalized generic covers. Once the generic global theorem in [F1] is instantiated, their classes are exactly the positive lower global vectors. Its induced quantum star therefore permutes these vectors with positive sign: $*G^-(b)=G^-(b^*)$. This is a consequence of the generic global theorem used here, not an input to its geometric or sign proof. [F1, F2]

2.1 Survival and non-merging. For a surviving normalized generic simple $S$, quotient Hom base change in the cover-descent lemma [F3] sends its normalized projective cover to the cyclotomic normalized cover, commutes with $\#$, and preserves its unscaled head pairing; if its simple is killed, the quotient is zero, because any nonzero finite quotient of the cover has a simple head and adjunction would produce a surviving generic head of the original cover. Thus raw extension of a generic normalized indecomposable projective is zero or a single normalized indecomposable cyclotomic projective, and distinct surviving heads do not merge; the image is $\pi_\Lambda G^-(b^*)$ respectively $G^-_\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda b^*)$ under the projections of [F1]. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, F3]

3.1 RIGHT-simple labels. The FIRST-block coefficient-$1$ expansion and LEFT-string ideal equality of [F4] identify the maximal FIRST-block partition of each generic cover with the adapted LEFT-string partition of its lower global vector. The one-step simple recursion increases this FIRST-string position by one; the adapted quantum recursion does the same. Induction on lowering paths from the vacuum therefore identifies the FIRST-end simple label with the ordinary canonical label. The mirror equivalence exchanges FIRST and RIGHT head/socle shift orbits, fixes the vacuum and induces star on the normalized cover class, so in the canonical RIGHT-simple label $c$ the equality is $\gamma^{-1}[P(S_c)]=G^-(c^*)$. The raw extension formula of step 1.1 cancels the two stars and sends it to $G^-_\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda c)$, with exactly the survivor label of [F3]. Every normalized cyclotomic cover is obtained because every cyclotomic simple inflates to a generic simple whose cover descends. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the generic global-basis and quantum-projection contracts of [F1] and the canonical-extraction supplier of [F3]; no other step uses infinite choice. The claim concerns indecomposable projectives, not every finite projective quotient. [step 1.2, step 2.1, F1, F2, F3, F4] ∎

items.title: Self-dual indecomposable cyclotomic projectives give the lower global basis
items.statement:
For a symmetric Cartan datum normalized by $d_i=1$, over any
characteristic-zero field, and the SAME finite loopless quiver with arbitrary
edge multiplicities and $Q_{ij}=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ as the
generic global theorem, use the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand quotient and
RIGHT append. The vacuum-normalized isomorphism
$\phi:K_0(\mathrm{Proj}\,R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ maps the classes of
normalized $\#$-self-dual indecomposable cyclotomic projectives bijectively
onto the lower global basis. The normalization is by projective HOM duality and
normalized simple heads, not by finite vector duality or a half-trace shift.
The projective with RIGHT crystal label $c\in B(\Lambda)$ maps to
$G^-_\Lambda(c)$. Every such projective is the surviving extension of a
generic normalized cover, with the raw map $\pi_\Lambda\circ*$ and the
FIRST/RIGHT label cancellation proved in the based-quotient lemma. The
uniqueness is at the level of normalized indecomposable projective isomorphism
classes; this is not an assertion that its generic lift is unique. No
arbitrary-parameter based extension is asserted.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** map each normalized cyclotomic cover to its based-quotient
class, show injectivity by the free normalized basis, and show surjectivity by
lifting lower global vectors through the generic theorem.

1.1 Cover classes land on lower global vectors. By [F1] all normalized cyclotomic covers are precisely the nonzero extensions of normalized generic covers, with distinct surviving simple heads; the based-quotient lemma sends each such class to a single positive lower global vector of $V_A(\Lambda)$, with no grading ambiguity because Hom base change preserves the $\#$-normalization and the degree-zero head pairing. [F1]

2.1 Surjectivity. Conversely the quantum global projection theorem [F2] supplies a generic global vector lifting every lower global vector of $V_A(\Lambda)$, and the generic theorem supplies its normalized generic cover; mirroring if necessary to use the raw first/right convention, its extension has that nonzero class and is a normalized indecomposable cover. Hence the assignment is surjective onto the lower basis. [step 1.1, F2]

3.1 Bijectivity and labels. The integral $K_0$ isomorphism and its free normalized projective basis make the assignment injective; the RIGHT crystal label identification of [F3] shows that the projective with RIGHT label $c\in B(\Lambda)$ maps to $G^-_\Lambda(c)$, with the FIRST/RIGHT label cancellation proved in the based-quotient lemma. The uniqueness is at the level of normalized indecomposable projective isomorphism classes, not of generic lifts, and no arbitrary-parameter based extension is asserted. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the generic global-basis and projection contracts of [F2]. [step 2.1, F1, F2, F3] ∎

items.title: Self-dual simple cyclotomic modules give the upper global basis
items.statement:
In exactly the symmetric normalized-$d_i=1$, characteristic-zero, loopless
arbitrary-multiedge geometric-parameter regime of the lower projective theorem,
the CANONICAL restricted-dual identification
$\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}:G_0(R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)^\vee$ maps normalized
$D_\psi$-self-dual simple classes bijectively to the upper global basis,
form-dual to the lower projective basis under the actual highest-weight
contravariant form. A simple and its normalized projective COVER have the same
$B(\Lambda)$ label; this is the cover/simple correspondence, not projective Hom
duality applied to a simple. Canonical $G_0$ operators have the same projective
normalization. The alternative KK module action remains valid, but its
intertwiner is
$\Psi_{\mathrm{KK}}=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}
\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}$ on root $\beta$ and sends a simple to that defect-rescaled
upper vector. The unrescaled upper-basis claim is made only for
$\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The geometric-parameter regime of the lower projective theorem, the
normalized $D_\psi$-self-dual simples and normalized covers, and the two
restricted-dual identifications.

[F1] The quotient-cover pairing
([[lem-cyclotomic-projective-covers-and-dualities-descend-through-the-quotient]]):
$T(P(S),S')=\delta_{S,S'}$ in normalized bases.

[F2] The lower projective theorem
([[thm-self-dual-indecomposable-cyclotomic-klr-projectives-give-the-lower-global-basis]]):
$\phi(P(S))$ is the lower global vector with the same crystal label.

[F3] The integral projective and $G_0$ identifications
([[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]],
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]])
and the upper/lower duality and crystal compatibility
([[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]],
[[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]],
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** pair the normalized simple functional against the lower
basis, identify it with the form-dual lower functional, and apply the
upper/lower duality theorem; then compare the two normalizations.

1.1 The functional $\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}(S)$. By [F1] the pairing is diagonal in normalized bases, and by [F2] the class $\phi(P(S))$ is the lower global vector with the same crystal label; therefore $\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}(S)$ is exactly the weightwise dual lower-basis functional with that label. [F1, F2]

2.1 Identification with the upper global basis. The integral projective identification [F3] identifies the tensor form on projectives with the actual highest-weight contravariant form; the upper/lower duality theorem identifies these restricted dual functionals with the upper global vectors and preserves crystal labels. This proves the bijection and the normalization statements, using neither a generic negative-half form nor a vector-dual trace shift. [step 1.1, F3]

3.1 Cover/simple correspondence and the two actions. A simple and its normalized projective cover have the same $B(\Lambda)$ label by the cover/simple correspondence of [F2], not by applying projective Hom duality to a simple. The $G_0$ theorem [F3] proves the canonical action and its defect-rescaled KK version; keeping the two maps distinct preserves both sound quantum actions and the rank-one $\lambda=2$ check, with $\Psi_{\mathrm{KK}}=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}$ on root $\beta$, so that only $\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}$ gives the unrescaled upper-basis claim. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the QG-5 global-basis duality and the generic basis suppliers of [F2] and [F3]. [step 2.1, F2, F3] ∎

title: Cyclotomic KLR Algebras and Highest-Weight Categorification — Examples

items.title: Cyclotomic KLR quotients in ranks zero, one and two
items.statement:
Work over any field $k$ with a real symmetrizable Cartan datum, arbitrary symmetrizers $d_i$, dominant $\Lambda$ and the STANDARD homogeneous polynomials $a_i=u^{\lambda_i}$.
(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$ has one normalized simple and projective, the vacuum.
(b) For every color $i$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ with $\deg x=2d_i$ and graded dimension $\sum_{r=0}^{\lambda_i-1}q^{2d_ir}$ when $\lambda_i\ge1$. Its unique normalized simple is $k$, its normalized projective HOM-self-dual cover is the regular module, and the coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda_i-1}$ Frobenius FUNCTIONAL has degree $-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$. If $\lambda_i=0$ the block is zero and has NO simple; if $\lambda_i=1$ it is $k$.
(c) In rank one $I=\{i\}$, at EVERY $n\ge0$ the algebra is the cyclotomic nil-Hecke quotient $NH_n/(x_1^{\lambda_i})$. It is nonzero precisely for $0\le n\le\lambda_i$. At each such root it has exactly one normalized self-dual simple, and zero blocks have none; hence there are $\lambda_i+1$ normalized simple classes in total, matching the rank-one highest-weight module. For $1\le n\le\lambda_i$ its symmetric corner is $k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]/(h_{\lambda_i-n+1},\ldots,h_{\lambda_i})$, the graded Grassmannian coinvariant ring, and the algebra is the associated graded polynomial-column matrix algebra. The normalized simple column has graded dimension $[n]_{q_i}!$, where $q_i=q^{d_i}$.
(d) Explicitly at $\lambda_i=2,n=2$, the block is $\operatorname{End}_k(C\{-d_i\})$ with $C=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$, its basis $1,x_1$ in degrees $0,2d_i$. Its unique self-dual simple $S_2=C\{-d_i\}$ has graded dimension $q_i^{-1}+q_i$ and is also the normalized indecomposable projective $P_2$. It is NOT a one-dimensional module with both dots zero. The regular class is $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=[2]_{q_i}[P_2]$ in $K_0$ and $[2]_{q_i}[S_2]$ in $G_0$.
(e) Arbitrary monic $a_i$ gives the ungraded deformation: $\lambda_i=2$, $a_i=u(u-1)$ gives $k\oplus k$ at root $\alpha_i$. Ordinary finiteness/symmetry remain true, but this is not the standard graded $V(2)$ identification.
items.strategy: compute the nil-Hecke first-power ideal as a matrix-entry ideal over the symmetric polynomials, using a finite companion algebra and its unit trace-dual basis; then identify the unique graded simple column and the explicit rank-two block.

items.title: Self-dual shift normalization for a cyclotomic projective
items.statement:
For rank one $d_i=1$ and $\lambda\ge1$, let $B=k[x]/x^\lambda$ and $P=B$. The PROJECTIVE Hom dual satisfies $P^\#\cong P$, so the canonical normalized projective is $P$ with no shift. Its finite vector dual is different:
$$D_\psi P\cong P\{-2(\lambda-1)\}.$$
The unique vector-dual-centered shift of this regular module is $P\{-(\lambda-1)\}$. For $\lambda=1$ both centers agree; for $\lambda=2$, projective Hom-self-duality centers $P$ at $0$ while vector-self-duality centers it at $-1$. If $\lambda=0$ the block is zero and there is no indecomposable projective here. For any normalized cyclotomic projective the general relation is $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)\}$; it does not redefine the lower-basis projective normalization.
items.strategy: Evaluation $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B,B)\cong B$ gives the projective dual directly, with the generator-fixing anti-involution producing the same left module. The coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda-1}$ trace has degree $-2(\lambda-1)$ and its perfect anti-diagonal pairing identifies $D_\psi B$ with $B$ in that NEGATIVE shift. Since $D_\psi(P\{s\})=D_\psi P\{-s\}$, vector self-duality solves $-2(\lambda-1)-s=s$, namely $s=-(\lambda-1)$. Projective Hom self-duality instead solves $-s=s$, namely $s=0$. These distinct finite calculations establish uniqueness of each center and their stated examples. The symmetric-algebra theorem gives the general defect shift after the independent projective normalization; no trace halving is used to pick the lower-basis class.

items.title: The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ commutator in a small cyclotomic weight
items.statement:
Take $I=\{i\}$ with $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2$, $d_i=1$, $q_i=q$, and
$\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$, so that $\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle=2$ and the standard
cyclotomic quotient has relations $x_1^2e(\nu)=0$. Then:

(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]/(x_1^2)$ with graded
dimension $1+q^2$, and $R^\Lambda(n\alpha_i)=0$ for $n\ge3$, so the functors
on the nonzero weights are $F^\Lambda_ik=R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)$ and
$F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_ik=0$;

(b) the categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relation of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-sl-two-categorical-commutator]] at $\beta=0$,
$\lambda=\Lambda$ (case $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle=2\ge0$) reads
$q^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\mathrm{Id}\oplus q^2\mathrm{Id}\cong
E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$; on the vacuum it says
$E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_ik\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$, which is exactly
$R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$;

(c) consequently, with the normalized operators of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]],
on $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda(0))]$: $E_iF_i[1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$
and $F_iE_i[1_\Lambda]=0$, so
$[E_i,F_i][1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]
=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$ with
$K_i[1_\Lambda]=q^2[1_\Lambda]$; on $[\mathrm{Rep}(R^\Lambda(0))]$ the same
commutator identity holds: $F_i[k]=q^{-1}[k\oplus k\{2\}]$, $E_i$ lowers back,
$F_iE_i[k]=0$, and $E_iF_i[k]=(q+q^{-1})[k]$. This is the mixed relation of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]]
verified at the first nontrivial weight.

items.title: Word projectives need not give lower global basis vectors
items.statement:
Once the isomorphism $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(\Lambda)$ of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]]
is known, the classes of the word projectives $R^\Lambda(\beta)e(\nu)$ are
automatically lower global basis vectors.
items.strategy:
At root $2\alpha_i$ the regular word projective has the graded decomposition
$$R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)\cong P_{i,2}\{1\}\oplus P_{i,2}\{-1\},\qquad [R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=(q+q^{-1})[P_{i,2}].$$

Under the vacuum-normalized identification the word class is $F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}$, whereas the lower global vector is $F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}$. Their ratio $q+q^{-1}$ is a nonunit of $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. The normalized indecomposable divided-power projective gives the lower vector in this weight; the ordinary word projective does not.

1.1 The word class. By [F1] the word projective decomposes as $(q+q^{-1})$ copies of $P_{i,2}$, so $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=(q+q^{-1})[P_{i,2}]$; under the K_0 isomorphism of the integral projective theorem this is the class of the ordinary product $F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}$. [F1]

1.2 In the rank-one module $V(2\Lambda_1)$, the Kashiwara string is $v,F_iv,F_i^{(2)}v$. These vectors generate its zero chart; they are bar fixed and generate the corresponding infinity chart. In weight $2\alpha_i$ the divided-power integral lattice is $AF_i^{(2)}v$: any divided word of that weight is an $A$-multiple of $F_i^{(2)}v$, since $F_i^2v=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$. Since an integral Laurent polynomial regular at both $0$ and infinity is an integer constant, the balanced intersection in that weight is $\mathbb ZF_i^{(2)}v$, and its positive string residue selects $F_i^{(2)}v$ as the lower global lift. [F2, algebra]

2.1 By [F2], $F_i^2v=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$. The coefficient $[2]_i=q+q^{-1}$ is a nonunit: evaluation at $q=1$ sends it to $2$, while an invertible Laurent polynomial must evaluate to a unit of $\mathbb Z$. Hence the word class cannot be the lower global vector identified in step 1.2. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F2, algebra]

3.1 This refutes the assertion that word-projective classes are automatically lower global vectors. Here the integral divided-power class $[P_{i,2}]$ gives $F_i^{(2)}v$ directly, whereas the regular word class has the nonunit coefficient $q+q^{-1}$. The finite example makes no general impossibility claim about extracting a basis from additional categorical or quantum-module structure. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: The projective-simple Cartan pairing in a small cyclotomic block
items.statement:
For rank one $d_i=1$, $\lambda=2$, let $B_r=R^\Lambda(r\alpha_i)$. The
normalized simples are $S_0=k$, $S_1=k$ with $x=0$, and
$S_2=C\{-1\}$ of graded dimension $q^{-1}+q$, where
$C=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$. Their normalized projective covers are
$P_0=k$, $P_1=k[x]/x^2$, $P_2=S_2$. Then $T(P_r,S_s)=\delta_{rs}$, with
distinct roots paired by zero. Under the integral projective identification
$P_0,P_1,P_2$ map to $v,Fv,F^{(2)}v$, respectively, while
$[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[P_2]$ maps to $F^2v$. In $G_0$ the correct regular classes
are $[B_1]=(1+q^2)[S_1]$ and $[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[S_2]$. The canonical
restricted-dual map sends $S_r$ to the form-dual of the corresponding divided
lower vector; it does not identify $B_1$ with $S_1$.
